endpoints.purpose: List documents authored in this agent's chat sessions (Document joined to Session.crew_member_id), newest first, max 200
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: an owned agent. curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/documents. Expect 200 {"documents": []} for a fresh agent — empty list is the cheap happy path. For a populated check, a document must exist in a session whose crew_member_id equals the agent id; items then have {id, session_id, session_name, title, language, preview (500 chars), version_count, created_at, updated_at}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown agent_id -> 404 'Agent not found'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Filters is_active=true and archived=false. Populated-path fixture requires running a chat as that agent that creates a document — an LLM-dependent setup, so prefer asserting the empty shape.

endpoints.purpose: List one directory level of an agent's on-disk sandbox workspace (data/agents/<id>/)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a CrewMember (agent) owned by the logged-in user must exist — create via the crew routes (POST under /api/agents from crew_routes.py) and capture its id. Then: curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/files' (optional query ?path=subdir). Expect 200 {"path": "", "entries": []} — workspace_root() creates the folder on demand, so an empty entries list is the valid fresh-agent happy path. Entries have {name, is_dir, size, mtime} sorted dirs-first.
endpoints.bad_input: ?path=../../etc -> 400 'Path is outside the workspace'. Unknown agent_id -> 404 'Agent not found'. ?path=<a file> -> 400 'Not a directory'. ?path=nonexistent-dir -> 404 'Path not found'.
endpoints.notes: Explicit 401 if no current_user (raised in route, independent of middleware). Owner-checked via crew_service.find_agent — another user's agent returns 404. Side effect: creates data/agents/<id>/ directory if missing.

endpoints.purpose: Read one text file from the agent's sandbox, path-confined and capped at 200,000 chars
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned agent (as above) plus a file in its workspace — simplest is to write data/agents/<agent_id>/hello.txt on disk (or have the agent's write_file tool create one). Then: curl -b cookies.txt 'http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/files/read?path=hello.txt'. Expect 200 {"path": "hello.txt", "name": "hello.txt", "size": <bytes>, "mtime": iso8601Z, "binary": false, "truncated": false, "content": "<file text>"}. Binary files return binary:true with empty content.
endpoints.bad_input: Omit the required 'path' query param -> 422 validation error. ?path=missing.txt -> 404 'File not found'. ?path=../outside -> 400 'Path is outside the workspace'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only; content truncated at 200k chars with truncated:true. Symlink-escape attempts are rejected by resolve_in_workspace.

endpoints.purpose: List gallery images generated in this agent's sessions, newest first, max 200
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: an owned agent. curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/images. Expect 200 {"images": []} for a fresh agent. Populated items (via gallery_helpers._image_to_dict or fallback) include {id, filename, url '/api/generated-image/<filename>', prompt, session_id, session_name, created_at}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown agent_id -> 404 'Agent not found'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Populated path requires image generation in an agent-bound session — assert the empty shape instead.

endpoints.purpose: List deep-research reports produced in this agent's sessions, read from data/deep_research/<session_id>.json files
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: an owned agent. curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/agents/<agent_id>/research. Expect 200 {"research": []} when the agent has no sessions or no report files. Populated items: {session_id, research_id, query, status, source_count, preview (cleaned, 280 chars), started_at, completed_at}, sorted newest first. To fake the populated path without an LLM: create a session with crew_member_id=<agent_id> and drop a matching <session_id>.json (keys: query, status, sources, result, started_at, completed_at, owner) into the research data dir.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown agent_id -> 404 'Agent not found'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only filesystem scan; reports owned by a different user (owner field in the JSON) are filtered out. Listing endpoint itself never triggers research — it only reads existing report files.

endpoints.purpose: Execute cleanup: archive sessions inactive >=7 days, delete archived non-important sessions inactive >=14 days with <10 messages
endpoints.test_plan: With any logged-in session: curl -X POST -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/cleanup (no body). Expect 200 {"archived_count": 0, "deleted_count": 0, "space_freed_mb": 0.0} on a fresh instance (nothing is old enough to touch). No fixtures needed for the no-op happy path.
endpoints.bad_input: Unauthenticated -> 401 from middleware; otherwise no body validation (body ignored).
endpoints.notes: Mutating but safe on fresh data: only sessions whose last_accessed predates the 7/14-day cutoffs are affected, top-30 recent and keyword-protected ('important','remember','save this','keep','bookmark' in name) sessions are preserved. Owner-scoped. Would silently archive/delete aged fixtures — run after time-sensitive session tests if you backdate timestamps.

endpoints.purpose: Dry-run preview of session cleanup: which sessions would be archived (inactive 7d) or deleted (archived, 14d+, <10 msgs, not important), plus estimated space
endpoints.test_plan: With any logged-in session: curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/cleanup/preview. Expect 200 JSON: {"sessions_to_archive": [], "sessions_to_delete": [], "preserved_sessions": [], "estimated_space_freed_mb": 0.0}. On a fresh instance all lists are empty (cutoffs are 7/14 days old) — that is the expected happy path. No fixtures needed.
endpoints.bad_input: No request validation to trip; unauthenticated call -> 401 from auth middleware.
endpoints.notes: Read-only, owner-scoped. Internal exceptions are swallowed in cleanup_service (returns empty preview), route wraps remaining errors as 500.

endpoints.purpose: Export all user data (memories, presets, skills, settings, features, preferences) as a downloadable JSON attachment
endpoints.test_plan: With an admin session cookie: curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/export. Expect 200, Content-Type application/json, Content-Disposition 'attachment; filename=odysseus_backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json'. Body is a JSON object with keys: version=1, exported_at, exported_by, memories (list), presets (dict), skills (list), settings (dict), features (dict), preferences (dict). No fixtures required — empty lists/dicts are fine on a fresh instance.
endpoints.bad_input: Call without an admin session (regular user cookie) -> 403 'Admin only'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Memories/skills are owner-filtered; presets are exported for all users. Save the response body to reuse as the /api/import fixture.

endpoints.purpose: Import a previously exported backup JSON; merges memories/skills (dedup by text/title/id), presets, settings, features, preferences into existing data
endpoints.test_plan: With an admin session: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"memories":[{"text":"imported test memory"}],"preferences":{"theme":"dark"}}' http://localhost:PORT/api/import. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "imported": ["1 memories", "preferences"], "message": "Imported: 1 memories, preferences"}. Re-posting the same body yields "0 memories" (duplicate text skipped). Best fixture: the body saved from GET /api/export.
endpoints.bad_input: POST with non-JSON body -> 400 'Invalid JSON'. POST a JSON array (e.g. '[]') -> 400 'Expected a JSON object'. POST '{}' -> 200 {"ok": false, "message": "No recognized data found in the file"}.
endpoints.notes: Side effects: writes memory store, skills store, presets file, and OVERWRITES matching keys in global settings.json and features flags (settings/features keys are dict.update-merged — importing {"settings":{...}} mutates server config for everyone). Run before settings-sensitive tests or restrict body to memories/skills/preferences.

endpoints.purpose: List all API tokens (metadata only — hash never returned)
endpoints.test_plan: With an admin session: curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/tokens. Expect 200 JSON array (empty on fresh install); after creating one, items have shape {"id", "name", "owner", "token_prefix" (8 chars 'ody_xxxx'), "scopes": ["chat"], "is_active": true, "last_used_at": null|iso, "created_at": iso}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'.
endpoints.notes: Lists tokens across all owners. Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new API bearer token (raw value 'ody_...' shown only in this response)
endpoints.test_plan: FORM-encoded, not JSON: curl -X POST -b cookies.txt -d 'name=test-token' http://localhost:PORT/api/tokens. Expect 200 {"id": <8-char uuid>, "name": "test-token", "owner": <admin username>, "token": "ody_<43 url-safe chars>", "token_prefix": <first 8 chars>, "scopes": ["chat"]}. Save id (for DELETE test) and token (the only time the raw value is revealed; usable as 'Authorization: Bearer ody_...' on scope-permitted routes).
endpoints.bad_input: POST with empty/missing name (curl -X POST -d 'name=') -> 400 'Token name is required'. Sending JSON instead of form data also yields 400 (name defaults to empty Form value).
endpoints.notes: Body must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart (FastAPI Form param). Name truncated to 100 chars. Side effects: inserts ApiToken row (bcrypt hash), invalidates the middleware token cache via app.state.invalidate_token_cache. Default scope is 'chat' only.

endpoints.purpose: Delete an API token by id
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: id from POST /api/tokens. curl -X DELETE -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/tokens/<id>. Expect 200 {"status": "deleted"}. A subsequent GET /api/tokens no longer lists it, and the deleted bearer token stops authenticating (cache invalidated).
endpoints.bad_input: DELETE /api/tokens/nonexistent -> 404 'Token not found'.
endpoints.notes: Pairs naturally with the create test (create -> list -> delete -> 404 on re-delete).

endpoints.purpose: Serve the SPA shell static/index.html (falls back to root index.html) with CSP nonce injected into {{CSP_NONCE}} placeholders
endpoints.test_plan: Logged-in session cookie required. curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/ → 200 text/html containing the app markup; the {{CSP_NONCE}} placeholder must be replaced with the per-request nonce. Unauthenticated → 302 redirect to /login (non-/api paths redirect instead of 401).
endpoints.notes: If neither static/index.html nor index.html exists → 404 "index.html not found". Same handler backs all SPA deep-link routes below.

endpoints.purpose: Serve a generated image/video file from data/generated_images by content-hash filename, with per-user ownership check against the gallery DB
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: place a file at data/generated_images/abcdef1234567890.png (filename must be 8-64 lowercase hex chars + allowed extension) and be logged in with a session cookie. Request: curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/generated-image/abcdef1234567890.png — expect 200 with Content-Type: image/png, raw image bytes, and header Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. If a GalleryImage DB row exists for that filename, its owner must match the logged-in user (mismatched owner returns 404); no row at all is allowed.
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/generated-image/evil.txt (fails regex ^[a-f0-9]{8,64}\.(png|jpg|jpeg|webp|gif|mp4|mov|webm|mkv|m4v)$) → 400 {"detail": "Invalid filename"}; a well-formed but nonexistent hash → 404 "Image not found"
endpoints.notes: Ownership enforcement only applies when a GalleryImage row exists AND get_current_user resolves (auth middleware sets request.state.current_user). Allowed extensions include video formats. Behind AuthMiddleware (not in exempt list) → unauthenticated /api/* request gets 401 {"error": "Not authenticated"}.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness check returning status + UTC timestamp
endpoints.test_plan: curl http://localhost:PORT/api/health → 200 {"status": "healthy", "timestamp": "<ISO-8601 UTC>"}. No auth, no fixtures.
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt; primary readiness probe for the whole test run.

endpoints.purpose: Report whether the server runs inside Docker and the effective Ollama base URL
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie (NOT auth-exempt): curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/api/runtime → 200 {"in_docker": false, "ollama_base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"} (URL varies with OLLAMA_BASE_URL/OLLAMA_URL env and Docker detection via /.dockerenv or /proc/1/cgroup). Unauthenticated → 401 {"error": "Not authenticated"}.
endpoints.notes: Read-only; does not contact Ollama, just computes the URL. Useful to verify auth middleware 401 behavior on /api/* paths.

endpoints.purpose: Return application version string
endpoints.test_plan: curl http://localhost:PORT/api/version → 200 {"version": "0.9.1"} (APP_VERSION from core/constants.py). No auth, no fixtures.
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt; good smoke-test endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Sandbox page for prototyping background visual effects (serves static/backgrounds.html with CSP nonce)
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /backgrounds → 200 text/html from static/backgrounds.html. NOTE: docstring claims 'No auth required' but the path is NOT in AUTH_EXEMPT_EXACT, so with AUTH_ENABLED=true an unauthenticated request gets 302 → /login. Test both ways and flag the docstring/middleware mismatch.
endpoints.notes: Docstring vs. middleware discrepancy worth a finding: page is effectively auth-gated despite the comment. 404-equivalent error if static/backgrounds.html is missing (open() raises → 500).

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Calendar view
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /calendar → 200 text/html (same as /). Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Cookbook tool
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /cookbook → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Email tool
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /email → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index. Serving the page needs no IMAP/SMTP creds (only the /api/email/* routes do).

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Gallery
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /gallery → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Library view
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /library → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: Serve the login/setup page (static/login.html) with CSP nonce injected
endpoints.test_plan: No cookie needed (in AUTH_EXEMPT_EXACT): curl http://localhost:PORT/login → 200 text/html containing the login form markup; {{CSP_NONCE}} replaced.
endpoints.notes: When no users are configured yet, all non-exempt non-/api paths 302-redirect here (first-run setup flow).

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Memory tool
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /memory → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend JS auto-opens the Notes modal based on pathname
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:PORT/notes → 200 text/html, identical body to / (delegates to serve_index). Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Pure alias for serve_index; testing one deep-link route plus / covers the code path, but all aliases should return 200.

endpoints.purpose: SPA deep-link: serves index.html; frontend auto-opens the Tasks view
endpoints.test_plan: With session cookie: GET /tasks → 200 text/html. Unauthenticated → 302 to /login.
endpoints.notes: Alias for serve_index.

endpoints.purpose: Verify a TOTP code to finish enabling 2FA; returns backup codes
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: same logged-in user after /2fa/setup; compute a current code from the returned secret (pyotp). POST /api/auth/2fa/confirm with {"code":"123456"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"backup_codes":[...]} (list of strings).
endpoints.bad_input: {"code":"000000"} (stale/wrong) -> 400 "Invalid code — try again"; no cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: 2FA becomes ENFORCED for this user's future logins (login then returns requires_totp). Disable via /2fa/disable in teardown or future logins for this user need totp_code.

endpoints.purpose: Disable 2FA for the current user, confirmed by password
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in user with 2FA enabled (after setup+confirm). POST /api/auth/2fa/disable with {"password":"hunter2pass"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true}; subsequent GET /api/auth/2fa/status shows {"enabled":false}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"password":"wrongpassword1"} -> 400 "Invalid password"; no cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Natural teardown for the 2FA test sequence.

endpoints.purpose: Generate a pending TOTP secret; returns secret, otpauth URI, and base64 QR PNG
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in user with 2FA NOT yet enabled. POST /api/auth/2fa/setup with empty body and session cookie. Expect 200 {"secret":"<base32>","uri":"otpauth://...","qr_code":"data:image/png;base64,..."}. Save the secret for the /2fa/confirm test (compute codes with pyotp.TOTP(secret).now()).
endpoints.bad_input: Calling again after 2FA is enabled -> 400 "2FA is already enabled"; no cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Requires the qrcode python package server-side. Side effect: stores a pending (unconfirmed) TOTP secret for the user. Use a dedicated test user so login fixtures for other tests don't suddenly require TOTP.

endpoints.purpose: Report whether 2FA is enabled for the current user
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/auth/2fa/status with a session cookie. Expect 200 {"enabled":false} on a fresh user (true after the confirm flow).
endpoints.bad_input: No cookie -> 401 "Not authenticated".
endpoints.notes: Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: Change the logged-in user's own password (requires current password)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in session cookie. POST /api/auth/change-password with {"current_password":"hunter2pass","new_password":"newhunter2pass"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. To keep fixtures stable, immediately change it back with a second call swapping the values.
endpoints.bad_input: {"current_password":"hunter2pass","new_password":"short"} -> 400 "Password must be at least 8 characters"; wrong current_password -> 400 "Current password is incorrect"; no cookie -> 401 "Not authenticated".
endpoints.notes: Side effect: persistent password change — restore afterwards or use a throwaway user created via admin POST /api/auth/users.

endpoints.purpose: Public read of UI feature-visibility toggles
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/auth/features with no cookie. Expect 200 with a flat dict of feature-name -> bool (contents of data features file).
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: Admin updates feature-visibility toggles
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. First GET /api/auth/features to learn valid keys, then POST /api/auth/features with e.g. {"<existing_key>":false}. Expect 200 returning the full updated dict with that key now false. Restore the original value afterwards.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin -> 403 "Admin only". Unknown keys and non-bool values are silently ignored (no error).
endpoints.notes: Only keys already present in the stored features file are writable, and only bool values. Side effect: persists to disk; toggle back in teardown.

endpoints.purpose: List configured third-party integrations with API keys masked (admin only)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. GET /api/auth/integrations. Expect 200 {"integrations":[{...,"api_key":"<masked>"}]} — empty list on a fresh install.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin -> 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: Read-only; api_key values are masked via mask_integration_secret.

endpoints.purpose: Admin creates a new integration (optionally from a preset)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. POST /api/auth/integrations with {"preset":"ntfy","name":"My ntfy","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8091","api_key":"","auth_type":"none"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"integration":{"id":"<12-hex>","enabled":true,"name":"My ntfy",...api_key masked}}. Save the id for update/delete/test calls. Cleanup with DELETE.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin -> 403. Body is unvalidated free-form JSON — even {} succeeds (defaults filled in), so no cheap 4xx besides auth.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: appends to data/integrations.json. Preset key merges preset defaults (auth_type/auth_header/description); unknown preset keys are ignored. id auto-generated if omitted.

endpoints.purpose: Public list of built-in integration presets (miniflux, gitea, linkding, homeassistant, ntfy, ...)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/auth/integrations/presets with no cookie. Expect 200 {"presets":{"miniflux":{"name":"Miniflux","auth_type":"header",...},"gitea":{...},"ntfy":{...}}} with any api_key fields omitted.
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Static read-only data.

endpoints.purpose: Admin deletes an integration
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + integration id from create. DELETE /api/auth/integrations/<id>. Expect 200 {"ok":true}; id no longer in GET /api/auth/integrations.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Integration not found"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary single-item CRUD delete (not DESTRUCTIVE).

endpoints.purpose: Admin updates fields on an existing integration
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + integration id from the create call. PUT /api/auth/integrations/<id> with {"name":"Renamed ntfy","enabled":false}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"integration":{...,"name":"Renamed ntfy","enabled":false}} with api_key masked.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id, e.g. PUT /api/auth/integrations/doesnotexist with {} -> 404 "Integration not found"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Free-form merge; 'id' in body is ignored (cannot be changed). Persists to data/integrations.json.

endpoints.purpose: Admin connectivity test: publishes a real ntfy message, or GETs a preset health endpoint (miniflux /v1/me, gitea /api/v1/version, linkding /api/tags/, homeassistant /api/, default /)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + an integration whose base_url points at a REACHABLE service. Easiest hermetic happy path: create integration {"preset":"ntfy","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8091"} with a local ntfy running, then POST /api/auth/integrations/<id>/test with empty body. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Sent to http://127.0.0.1:8091/reminders — ..."}. Without a reachable backend the endpoint still returns 200 but {"ok":false,"message":"...failed..."} — assert on the ok field, not the status code.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown integration id -> 404 "Integration not found"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Real outbound HTTP side effect: for ntfy it POSTs an actual notification to the topic from settings key reminder_ntfy_topic (default 'reminders') — subscribers WILL receive a test message. base_url path/query is stripped to scheme://host:port for ntfy. Other presets go through execute_api_call (uses stored api_key + auth_type). 8s httpx timeout for ntfy. Network failures are reported as ok:false with a 200, never 5xx.

endpoints.purpose: Password (+ optional TOTP) login; sets the odysseus_session cookie
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a user exists (e.g. admin from /setup). POST /api/auth/login with {"username":"admin","password":"hunter2pass","remember":true}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"username":"admin"} and a Set-Cookie header for odysseus_session (httponly, samesite=lax, max-age 604800 when remember=true). If the user has 2FA enabled and totp_code omitted, expect 200 {"ok":false,"requires_totp":true,"username":"admin"} — then retry with "totp_code":"123456".
endpoints.bad_input: Wrong password {"username":"admin","password":"wrongwrong1"} -> 401 "Invalid credentials"; wrong totp_code with 2FA on -> 401 "Invalid 2FA code".
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Rate limited: 15 requests / 60s per IP (429). Username is lowercased/stripped server-side. Cookie secure flag controlled by SECURE_COOKIES env var. This is the prerequisite fixture for every cookie-auth endpoint below — capture the cookie with curl -c.

endpoints.purpose: Revoke the current session token and clear the session cookie
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/auth/logout with the odysseus_session cookie from login (curl -b cookies.txt). Expect 200 {"ok":true} and a Set-Cookie deleting odysseus_session. Also succeeds with no cookie at all (idempotent).
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Side effect: invalidates the session token server-side — run last in a cookie-reusing test sequence or re-login afterwards.

endpoints.purpose: Read app settings — full set for admins, secret-scrubbed copy for everyone else
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/auth/settings with no cookie (or a non-admin cookie): expect 200 settings dict with secret-bearing keys blanked by scrub_settings. With an admin cookie: same dict but secrets present. Compare a known secret key (e.g. an API key field) between the two to verify scrubbing.
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware (frontend needs keybinds/TTS prefs pre-login). Read-only. Good place to assert no secret leakage to anonymous callers.

endpoints.purpose: Admin updates app settings (keys restricted to DEFAULT_SETTINGS)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. POST /api/auth/settings with a harmless known key from src/settings.DEFAULT_SETTINGS, e.g. {"reminder_ntfy_topic":"reminders-test"}. Expect 200 returning the full updated settings dict containing that value. Restore the previous value in teardown.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin -> 403 "Admin only". Keys not in DEFAULT_SETTINGS are silently dropped.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: persists settings to disk and can change global behavior (LLM endpoints, TTS, etc.) — mutate only innocuous keys and restore.

endpoints.purpose: First-run creation of the initial admin account (only when no accounts exist)
endpoints.test_plan: On a fresh instance (data/auth.json absent or empty users), POST /api/auth/setup with JSON {"username":"admin","password":"hunter2pass"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Admin account created"}. On an already-configured instance this endpoint is unusable for happy-path (returns 400 "Already configured"), so test it first or against a clean data dir.
endpoints.bad_input: Password under 8 chars, e.g. {"username":"admin","password":"short"} -> 400 "Password must be at least 8 characters"; if accounts already exist -> 400 "Already configured".
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Rate limited: 3 requests / 300s per client IP (429 after). Side effect: creates persistent admin user in data/auth.json — effectively one-shot per deployment. Run before any other auth test.

endpoints.purpose: Self-service account creation when admin has enabled open registration
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: instance configured (setup done) AND signup enabled (admin POST /api/auth/signup-toggle until status shows signup_enabled:true). Then POST /api/auth/signup with {"username":"alice","password":"alicepassword1"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Account created"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"username":"alice","password":"short"} -> 400 "Password must be at least 8 characters"; if signup disabled -> 403 "Registration is disabled..."; duplicate username -> 409 "Username already taken".
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Rate limited: 3 requests / 300s per IP (429). Side effect: persists a new non-admin user. Depends on /api/auth/signup-toggle state.

endpoints.purpose: Admin toggles open registration on/off
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. POST /api/auth/signup-toggle with empty body. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"signup_enabled":true} (or false — it flips). Confirm via GET /api/auth/status signup_enabled field. Toggle twice to restore original state.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin -> 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: Stateful flip-flop with no explicit set — tests must toggle back. Gates POST /api/auth/signup.

endpoints.purpose: Report auth configuration/login state, signup_enabled flag, and caller privileges
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/auth/status with no cookie: expect 200 JSON including "signup_enabled" (bool) and configured/authenticated state from auth_manager.status(). With a valid session cookie: response additionally includes "username" and "privileges" (dict of capability flags).
endpoints.notes: Auth-exempt in middleware. Read-only; good smoke test and used to verify login fixtures.

endpoints.purpose: Admin deletes a user account (body-specified username)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + throwaway user 'bob'. curl -X DELETE /api/auth/users -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"bob"}' with admin cookie. Expect 200 {"ok":true}; bob gone from GET /api/auth/users.
endpoints.bad_input: Deleting a protected target (e.g. yourself/last admin per auth_manager.delete_user rules) -> 400 "Cannot delete user"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Unusual: DELETE with a JSON body (some clients/proxies strip DELETE bodies). Ordinary single-item delete, not classed DESTRUCTIVE. CORS only allows GET/POST/PUT/DELETE so this works cross-origin.

endpoints.purpose: List all user accounts (admin only)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session cookie. GET /api/auth/users. Expect 200 {"users":[...]} (list from auth_manager.list_users()).
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin or no cookie -> 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Auth check reads the cookie directly (not request.state), so bearer API tokens and the internal-tool header do NOT work here — only an admin session cookie.

endpoints.purpose: Admin creates a new user account (optionally admin)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie. POST /api/auth/users with {"username":"bob","password":"bobpassword1","is_admin":false}. Expect 200 {"ok":true}; user appears in GET /api/auth/users. Cleanup via DELETE /api/auth/users.
endpoints.bad_input: {"username":"bob2","password":"short"} -> 400 "Password must be at least 8 characters"; existing username -> 409 "Username already taken"; non-admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: persists user to data/auth.json. Good way to mint throwaway users for the user-auth test suites.

endpoints.purpose: Admin sets a non-admin user's privilege flags
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + a non-admin user 'bob'. PUT /api/auth/users/bob/privileges with a raw JSON dict of boolean flags, e.g. {"shell":false,"email":true}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"privileges":{...merged effective set...}}. Verify via GET /api/auth/status as bob.
endpoints.bad_input: Target user missing OR target is an admin -> 404 "User not found or is admin"; non-admin caller -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Body is an unvalidated free-form dict (request.json()) passed to auth_manager.set_privileges — keys mirror DEFAULT_PRIVILEGES in core/auth.py. Admins cannot have privileges set (always full).

endpoints.purpose: Admin renames a user, migrating all owner-scoped DB rows and JSON prefs to the new name
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin cookie + throwaway user 'bob' (create via POST /api/auth/users). PUT /api/auth/users/bob/rename with {"username":"robert"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"username":"robert","renamed_self":false}. Same-name rename is a no-op 200. Verify 'robert' appears in GET /api/auth/users.
endpoints.bad_input: {"username":""} -> 400 "Username required"; unknown source user -> 404 "User not found"; target name taken -> 409 "Username already taken".
endpoints.notes: Heavy side effects: UPDATEs the owner column on EVERY SQLAlchemy model with an 'owner' attribute (sessions, docs, email accounts, tasks, ...) and rewrites per-user prefs JSON before renaming the auth record. Test only with throwaway users. Renaming the calling admin invalidates context (renamed_self flag). 500 "Failed to rename user data" if DB migration fails.

endpoints.purpose: List the caller's calendars (auto-creates a default 'Personal' calendar if none exist)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/calendar/calendars. Expect 200 {"calendars":[{"name":"Personal","href":"<uuid>","color":"#5b8abf"}]} on first call (default calendar is created as a side effect). href is the calendar id used by other endpoints.
endpoints.notes: Side effect on first call: inserts the default CalendarCal row for the owner.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new local calendar
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/calendars?name=Work&color=%23ff0000 (parameters are QUERY params, not JSON body; both optional, defaults name=Imported color=#5b8abf). Expect 200 {"ok":true,"id":"<uuid>","name":"Work","color":"#ff0000"}.
endpoints.notes: name/color are query parameters because they are plain function defaults, not a Pydantic body.

endpoints.purpose: Delete a calendar AND all events in it
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a throwaway calendar (POST /api/calendar/calendars?name=Temp) and optionally an event in it. DELETE /api/calendar/calendars/<id>. Expect 200 {"ok":true}; all CalendarEvent rows with that calendar_id are bulk-deleted first.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown cal_id → 404 "Calendar not found".
endpoints.notes: Deletes every event in the calendar — destructive at calendar scope but still single-entity CRUD; do NOT run against the user's default 'Personal' calendar in shared test envs. On non-HTTP exceptions it returns 200 {"error":"..."} instead of a 5xx.

endpoints.purpose: Rename or recolor an owned calendar
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a calendar, capture id. PUT /api/calendar/calendars/<id>?name=Renamed&color=%2300ff00 (query params). Expect 200 {"ok":true}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown or other-user cal_id → 404 "Calendar not found".
endpoints.notes: Query params, not body.

endpoints.purpose: Return the caller's saved CalDAV connection settings (password masked)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/calendar/config with a logged-in session cookie. Expect 200 JSON {"url":"","username":"","password":"","has_password":false,"local":true} on a fresh install (local:true when no CalDAV url saved). Password is always returned as empty string.
endpoints.notes: Reads per-user prefs via routes/prefs_routes._load_for_user. No side effects.

endpoints.purpose: Save (or clear) the caller's CalDAV url/username/password in prefs
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/config with JSON {"url":"https://dav.example.com/cal/","username":"bob","password":"secret"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. Follow-up GET /api/calendar/config shows url+username and has_password:true. Sending {} or {"url":""} clears the integration and returns {"ok":true,"cleared":true}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-JSON body is tolerated (parsed as {}), which clears the config — so the cheap negative test is: empty body returns {"ok":true,"cleared":true}, not an error.
endpoints.notes: Persists to per-user prefs. Empty password in body preserves previously stored password. No validation of the URL itself (use /test for that).

endpoints.purpose: List events overlapping a [start,end) window, expanding RRULE recurrences server-side
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create an event via POST /api/calendar/events. Then GET /api/calendar/events?start=2026-06-01&end=2026-07-01 (optional &calendar=<id or name>). Expect 200 {"events":[{uid,summary,dtstart,dtend,all_day,is_utc,description,location,rrule,calendar,calendar_href,color,event_type,importance,is_recurrence,series_uid}, ...]} sorted by dtstart. Recurring events appear as occurrences with compound uid "<base>::2026-06-15T12:00".
endpoints.bad_input: Unparseable range (start=NaN-NaN-NaN) → 200 {"events":[]} (logged, intentionally not an error). Missing start/end query params → 422.
endpoints.notes: start/end accept ISO dates or natural language ('today', 'next monday'). Excludes status='cancelled' events.

endpoints.purpose: Create a calendar event (defaults to the owner's default calendar)
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/events with JSON {"summary":"Lunch with Sara","dtstart":"2026-06-15T12:00:00","dtend":"2026-06-15T13:00:00","all_day":false,"location":"Downtown","description":""}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"uid":"<uuid>"}. Omitting dtend defaults to +1h (timed) or +1 day (all_day). Optional calendar_href targets a specific owned calendar; optional rrule (e.g. "FREQ=WEEKLY") and color.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing required field summary or dtstart → 422 from Pydantic. calendar_href belonging to another user → 404 "Calendar not found".
endpoints.notes: Tz-aware dtstart (Z or +HH:MM) is stored as UTC with is_utc=true and serialized back with a Z suffix.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one event (or a whole recurring series via its base/compound UID)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create an event, capture uid. DELETE /api/calendar/events/<uid>. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. Subsequent GET /events for the window no longer includes it.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown uid → 404 "Event not found"; uid "::x" → 400.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD.

endpoints.purpose: Update fields of an existing event; compound occurrence UIDs resolve to the series
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create an event, capture uid. PUT /api/calendar/events/<uid> with JSON {"summary":"Renamed","location":"Office"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. All body fields optional (EventUpdate). A compound uid like <uid>::2026-06-15T12:00 edits the whole series (base uid).
endpoints.bad_input: uid starting with '::' → 400 "malformed compound UID: missing base before ::"; unknown uid → 404 "Event not found".
endpoints.notes: Setting all_day:true forces is_utc=false; tz-aware dtstart/dtend escalate is_utc to true.

endpoints.purpose: Export an owned calendar as a downloadable .ics file
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a calendar with at least one event (use GET /calendars for the default id, POST an event). GET /api/calendar/export/<cal_id>. Expect 200 with Content-Type text/calendar, Content-Disposition attachment filename="<Name>.ics", body starting BEGIN:VCALENDAR and containing one BEGIN:VEVENT per non-cancelled event.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown/other-user cal_id → 404 "Calendar not found".
endpoints.notes: Hand-rolled ICS serialization; RRULE and DESCRIPTION included when present.

endpoints.purpose: Import events from an uploaded .ics file into a (possibly new) calendar
endpoints.test_plan: multipart/form-data POST /api/calendar/import with file field 'file' containing a small ICS (BEGIN:VCALENDAR / VEVENT with DTSTART/DTEND/SUMMARY / END:VCALENDAR); optional QUERY param calendar_name=TestImport. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"imported":1,"skipped":0,"calendar":"TestImport","calendar_id":"<uuid>"}. Re-importing the same file skips duplicates (same dtstart+summary in target calendar).
endpoints.bad_input: Non-ICS file content → 400 "Invalid ICS file: ..."; file >10MB → 413; missing file field → 422.
endpoints.notes: File upload (multipart), 10MB hard cap (_ICS_MAX_BYTES). calendar_name is a query param (not Form). Creates a calendar with source='import' color #7c4dff if the name doesn't exist. Fresh UUIDs are assigned per imported event.

endpoints.purpose: List the caller's .ics feed subscriptions
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/calendar/subscriptions. Expect 200 {"subscriptions":[]} on fresh install, or entries {"id":"ics-<24 hex>","url":"https://...","name":"..."} after POSTing one. id is sha256(url)[:24] prefixed with 'ics-'.
endpoints.notes: Reads prefs['ics_subs'].

endpoints.purpose: Add/update an .ics feed subscription — validates by fetching and parsing the feed first
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/subscriptions with JSON {"url":"https://example.com/schedule.ics","name":"Uni"}. Requires the URL to return HTTP 200 with valid VCALENDAR content (serve a small .ics from a local HTTP server for the fixture). Expect 200 {"ok":true,"id":"ics-<24hex>","name":"Uni","events":<VEVENT count>}. webcal:// URLs are rewritten to https://. Optional replace_id swaps an existing entry and deletes its synced calendar.
endpoints.bad_input: {"url":"ftp://x"} → 200 {"ok":false,"error":"URL must be http(s):// or webcal://"}; an http URL serving non-ICS → {"ok":false,"error":"Not a valid iCalendar feed: ..."}.
endpoints.notes: Outbound httpx GET with 15s timeout (under the 45s global request timeout). Persists to prefs['ics_subs']; may delete a replaced synced calendar row + its events.

endpoints.purpose: Remove an .ics subscription and its synced local calendar + events
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: POST a subscription first and capture the returned id. DELETE /api/calendar/subscriptions/ics-<24hex>. Expect 200 {"ok":true}. The synced CalendarCal row with that id (and its events, via cascade) is deleted.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown sub_id → 404 {"detail":"Subscription not found"}.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one; cascades the feed's synced events.

endpoints.purpose: Pull events from the configured CalDAV account and all .ics feed subscriptions into local SQLite
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/sync with empty body. With a CalDAV account or .ics subscription configured in prefs, expect 200 with merged counts {"calendars":N,"events":N,"deleted":N,"errors":[]}. With nothing configured, still 200: {"calendars":0,"events":0,"deleted":0,"errors":["No calendar sources configured"]} — that unconfigured response is the cheap no-creds smoke test.
endpoints.notes: Delegates to src/caldav_sync.sync_caldav(owner). Side effect: upserts CalendarCal/CalendarEvent rows. Also invoked by frontend on calendar open and the periodic scheduler. Outbound HTTP to CalDAV/ics URLs.

endpoints.purpose: Probe a CalDAV server with a PROPFIND handshake (test-before-save)
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/calendar/test with JSON {"url":"https://dav.example.com/cal/","username":"bob","password":"secret"}. With a reachable CalDAV server responding 207/200 to PROPFIND, expect 200 {"ok":true}. Falls back to saved creds when body fields are missing. All failures still return HTTP 200 with {"ok":false,"error":"..."} (e.g. "Auth failed — check username/password" on 401, "Connection timed out").
endpoints.bad_input: POST {} with no saved config → 200 {"ok":false,"error":"Missing URL, username, or password"}.
endpoints.notes: Makes an outbound httpx PROPFIND with 8s timeout; needs a real CalDAV endpoint (e.g. local Radicale) for the happy path. No DB writes.

endpoints.purpose: Add a new contact (PUT vCard to CardDAV or append to local JSON)
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/contacts/add with JSON {"name":"Sara Lee","email":"sara@example.com"}. Expect 200 {"success":true}. Re-adding the same email → 200 {"success":true,"message":"Already exists","contact":{...}}. Name defaults to the email local-part when omitted.
endpoints.bad_input: {} or missing email → 200 {"success":false,"error":"Email required"}.
endpoints.notes: With CardDAV configured this does an outbound httpx PUT of a generated vCard (becomes EXTERNAL-CREDS-dependent); local mode writes data/contacts.json. Invalidates contact cache.

endpoints.purpose: Return CardDAV connection settings with password masked
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/contacts/config → 200 {"url":"","username":"","password":""} on fresh install; password is "***" when one is stored. Values come from data/settings.json falling back to env CARDDAV_URL/CARDDAV_USERNAME/CARDDAV_PASSWORD.
endpoints.notes: Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: Save CardDAV url/username/password into data/settings.json
endpoints.test_plan: PUT /api/contacts/config with JSON {"carddav_url":"http://localhost:5232/user/contacts/","carddav_username":"user","carddav_password":"pw"} → 200 {"success":true}. Only the three carddav_* keys are read; others ignored. Follow-up GET /config reflects the new url. To restore local-only mode, PUT {"carddav_url":""}.
endpoints.notes: Writes data/settings.json (shared global settings file, not per-user) and invalidates the contact cache. No connectivity validation is performed.

endpoints.purpose: Export all contacts as a downloadable .vcf or .csv
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/contacts/export?format=csv → 200, Content-Type text/csv, Content-Disposition attachment filename="odysseus-contacts.csv", header row name,email,phone. Default format=vcf returns text/vcard with concatenated BEGIN:VCARD blocks.
endpoints.bad_input: format=xml → 422 (Query pattern ^(vcf|csv)$).
endpoints.notes: Forces a fresh fetch (cache bypass).

endpoints.purpose: Bulk-import contacts from a vCard blob or CSV text in the JSON body
endpoints.test_plan:
POST /api/contacts/import with JSON {"vcf":"BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:4.0
FN:Bob Jones
EMAIL:bob@example.com
END:VCARD"}. Expect 200 {"imported":1,"failed":0,"total":1,"success":true}. CSV variant: {"csv":"name,email,phone
Bob Jones,bob@example.com,+1555"} → same shape. Duplicate emails are skipped (success false if nothing new imported).
endpoints.bad_input: {} → 200 {"success":false,"error":"No contact data found"}; {"vcf":"hello"} → {"success":false,"error":"No vCard data found"}.
endpoints.notes: Body is JSON (not multipart). vCard path preserves full card content; CSV path supports header sniffing and falls back to positional name,email,phone columns. With CardDAV configured, each card is an outbound PUT (15s timeout each — large imports could approach the 45s global request timeout); CSV phone numbers trigger an extra update PUT per row.

endpoints.purpose: List all contacts (CardDAV when configured, else local data/contacts.json)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/contacts/list with an admin session cookie. Expect 200 {"contacts":[{"uid","name","emails":[],"phones":[]}...],"count":N} (empty list + count 0 on fresh install). Non-admin session → 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: 60s in-memory cache (_contact_cache). Without CardDAV config this is purely local-file backed — no external deps.

endpoints.purpose: Substring search of contacts by name or email, max 10 results
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: POST /api/contacts/add {"name":"Sara Lee","email":"sara@example.com"} first. GET /api/contacts/search?q=sara → 200 {"results":[{"uid","name":"Sara Lee","emails":["sara@example.com"],"phones":[]}]}. Empty/missing q → {"results":[]}.
endpoints.notes: Case-insensitive substring match; capped at 10.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one contact by UID
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: add a contact, get its uid from /list. DELETE /api/contacts/<uid> → 200 {"success":true}; contact no longer appears in /list. In local mode deleting a non-existent uid still returns success:true (filter semantics); in CardDAV mode a remote 404 is also treated as success.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD (not classed DESTRUCTIVE). CardDAV mode issues an outbound DELETE to the resolved resource URL.

endpoints.purpose: Edit an existing contact's name/emails/phones (rewrites the vCard or local row)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: add a contact, then find its uid via GET /api/contacts/list. PUT /api/contacts/<uid> with JSON {"name":"Sara L. Lee","emails":["sara@example.com","s.lee@work.com"],"phones":["+1 555 0100"]} → 200 {"success":true}. Legacy single "email" key also accepted. In local mode an unknown uid is upserted (still success:true).
endpoints.bad_input: Body with neither name nor emails ({"phones":["+1"]}) → 200 {"success":false,"error":"Name or email required"}.
endpoints.notes: Declared after the literal routes so /config, /list etc. take precedence. With CardDAV configured this PUTs to the resolved resource href (outbound HTTP).

endpoints.purpose: List IANA timezone names for the settings dropdown
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/assistant/available-timezones with a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 {"timezones": [...sorted IANA names...]} containing e.g. "America/New_York" and "UTC".
endpoints.bad_input: No session cookie -> 401 from auth middleware.
endpoints.notes: No per-user logic; auth comes only from the global AuthMiddleware. Falls back to ["UTC"] if zoneinfo unavailable.

endpoints.purpose: Report whether the most recent TaskRun of a scheduled task has finished
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a task_id owned by the current user (from /api/assistant/settings). GET /api/assistant/run-status/<task_id>. Success: 200 with {"status": "unknown"} (never run), {"status": "running"}, or {"status": "done", "result_status": "..."} — all valid.
endpoints.bad_input: task_id belonging to another user or nonexistent -> 404 'Task not found'.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Works on any of the user's scheduled tasks, not only assistant check-ins (only the run endpoint enforces the crew check).

endpoints.purpose: Resolve (lazily creating) the per-user default-assistant CrewMember and its pinned chat session
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in real user (not 'api'/'internal-tool' — synthetic owners are rejected 400). GET /api/assistant/session. Success: 200 {"session_id": "...", "crew_member_id": "...", "name": "..."}.
endpoints.bad_input: Bearer-token caller (current_user='api') -> 400 "Cannot seed assistant for 'api'". Unauthenticated -> 401.
endpoints.notes: SIDE EFFECT on first call per user: seeds a CrewMember + pinned Session + three daily check-in ScheduledTasks (Morning/Midday/Evening) via task_scheduler.ensure_assistant_defaults. Idempotent afterwards.

endpoints.purpose: Return the assistant CrewMember fields plus its three check-in scheduled tasks
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in user (assistant auto-seeds on this call). GET /api/assistant/settings. Success: 200 {"crew": {id,name,avatar,personality,model,endpoint_url,enabled_tools,session_id,is_default_assistant,timezone,allow_autonomous_email,...}, "check_ins": [{id,name,scheduled_time,prompt,enabled,next_run,last_run,run_count} x3], "task_ids": [...]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unauthenticated -> 401 'Not authenticated'.
endpoints.notes: Same lazy-seed side effect as /api/assistant/session. Save the returned check_in ids/task_ids — needed for run/{task_id}, run-status/{task_id}, and PATCH settings tests.

endpoints.purpose: Update assistant CrewMember fields and/or its check-in tasks (times, prompts, enabled) in one call
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: GET /api/assistant/settings first to get a check-in id. PATCH /api/assistant/settings JSON {"name": "Testy", "timezone": "America/New_York", "check_ins": [{"id": "<task_id>", "scheduled_time": "09:30", "enabled": false}]}. Success: 200 with refreshed {crew, check_ins, task_ids}; crew.name == "Testy", that check-in shows enabled:false and scheduled_time "09:30". Restore original values afterwards.
endpoints.bad_input: check_ins entry missing required 'id' -> 422 (pydantic CheckInUpdate). Unauthenticated -> 401.
endpoints.notes: All fields optional. allow_autonomous_email toggles send_email/reply_to_email in enabled_tools. Timezone or time changes recompute next_run for check-in tasks. Unknown check-in ids are silently skipped (no error). Mutates persistent scheduler state — restore after testing.

endpoints.purpose: Reconnect SSE subscription to a still-running detached chat/agent run
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: start a long-ish /api/chat_stream turn for an owned session, then while it is running: GET /api/chat/resume/<session_id>. Success: 200 text/event-stream replaying buffered events then live chunks through 'data: [DONE]'.
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/chat/resume/<owned-session-with-no-active-run> -> 404 'No active run for this session'. Other user's session id -> 404 (owner check).
endpoints.notes: SSE; read-only subscriber — does not start or consume LLM work itself. Timing-dependent: needs an in-flight run, so easiest tested together with a slow chat_stream prompt.

endpoints.purpose: Cancel a detached chat/agent run (Stop button)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned session (run optional). POST /api/chat/stop/<session_id> with empty body. Success: 200 {"stopped": true} if a run was active, {"stopped": false} otherwise — both are valid 200s, so the cheap happy path needs no active run.
endpoints.bad_input: Nonexistent/other-user session id -> 404 from _verify_session_owner.
endpoints.notes: Side effect: cancels the detached run; partial assistant response gets saved with stopped:true metadata by the stream's cancellation handler.

endpoints.purpose: Report whether a stream/run is active for a session (and partial text if tracked)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned session with an in-flight chat_stream. GET /api/chat/stream_status/<session_id>. Success: 200 with {"status":"streaming","partial":...,"query":...,...} or {"status":"streaming","detached":true}. With no active stream the documented behavior is 404 — treat 404 as the expected idle result.
endpoints.bad_input: Idle or unknown session -> 404 'No active stream for this session' / 404 owner check.
endpoints.notes: Read-only; pairs with chat_stream for testing. 404 on idle sessions is normal, not a failure.

endpoints.purpose: Append an untrusted 'research context' system-style message into a session's history
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned session. POST /api/inject_context/<session_id> as form-data with context="Paris is the capital of France". Success: 200 {"status": "context_injected"}; session history gains an injected context message (verify via session/history routes).
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'context' form field -> 422. Unknown session -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded (context: str = Form(...)). Side effect: writes a message into session history and saves sessions. No LLM call.

endpoints.purpose: Substring search across the current user's non-archived chat messages
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: at least one chat message containing a known token (e.g. send 'pong' via /api/chat first). GET /api/search?q=pong&limit=5. Success: 200 JSON array of {session_id, session_name, role, content_snippet, timestamp}; empty q returns [].
endpoints.bad_input: limit=0 -> 422 (Query ge=1); limit=101 -> 422 (le=100).
endpoints.notes: Read-only, scoped to DBSession.owner == current user. q='' returns empty list with 200, not an error.

endpoints.purpose: Report STT service provider/availability statistics
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/stt/stats with a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 JSON with at least {"available": bool, "provider": "disabled|browser|local|endpoint:<id>"}; provider-specific extras (model info, endpoint_id) when configured.
endpoints.bad_input: No auth cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Provider read from data/settings.json on each call; default stt_provider is 'disabled', so expect available:false on a fresh install — still a 200.

endpoints.purpose: Transcribe an uploaded audio file to text via the configured STT provider (local Whisper or API endpoint)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: stt_provider set to 'local' (downloads/loads a Whisper model) or 'endpoint:<id>' (configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint) in settings, plus a small audio file. Request: POST /api/stt/transcribe as multipart/form-data, field 'file' = e.g. a short WAV saying 'hello'. Success: 200 {"text": "hello..."}. On a default install (provider 'disabled'), expect 503 — record as expected-unavailable, not a failure.
endpoints.bad_input: Empty file upload -> 400 {"message": "Empty audio file"}. Provider disabled/browser -> 503 {"message": "STT service not available or set to browser mode"}. Missing 'file' field -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Multipart upload. 'local' provider needs the whisper model + torch (first call may exceed the 45s hard timeout while loading — /api/stt is NOT timeout-exempt); 'endpoint:' provider needs a working external API endpoint. Transcription failure -> 500.

endpoints.purpose: Clear the TTS synthesis cache
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/tts/clear-cache with empty body and a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 {"success": true, "message": "Cache cleared"}.
endpoints.bad_input: No auth cookie -> 401. (No request-body validation — any body is ignored.)
endpoints.notes: Side effect: deletes cached audio files; harmless and idempotent. Safe to run anytime.

endpoints.purpose: Report TTS service provider/availability statistics
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/tts/stats with a logged-in cookie. Success: 200 JSON with {"available": bool, "ready": bool, "provider": ...} plus model/cache details.
endpoints.bad_input: No auth cookie -> 401.
endpoints.notes: Default tts_provider is 'disabled' -> available:false but still 200.

endpoints.purpose: Synthesize speech from text via the configured TTS provider (local Kokoro or API endpoint), returning audio bytes or base64
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: tts_provider set to 'local' (Kokoro-82M loaded) or 'endpoint:<id>'. Request: POST /api/tts/synthesize JSON {"text": "Hello world", "format": "base64"}. Success: 200 {"audio": "<base64 string>"}. With format "audio" (default): 200 binary body, Content-Type audio/mpeg or audio/wav, Content-Disposition inline. On default install (disabled) expect 503 — record as expected-unavailable.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'text' -> 422 (pydantic). Provider disabled/browser -> 503 {"message": "TTS service not available"}. Synthesis returning nothing -> 500 {"message": "Synthesis failed"}.
endpoints.notes: Caches results keyed by provider/model/voice/text. Local Kokoro requires model + GPU/CPU runtime; first synthesis can be slow and /api/tts is not exempt from the 45s hard timeout. format values other than 'base64' fall through to binary audio.

endpoints.purpose: Probe GPU memory/utilization/processes via nvidia-smi, AMD sysfs, or /dev device holders (local or SSH)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/cookbook/gpus with admin session, no params. On a GPU-less box (e.g. mac) expect 200 {"ok": false, "error": "nvidia-smi not found" (or similar), "gpus": []}. On NVIDIA box expect 200 {"ok": true, "backend": "cuda", "source": "nvidia-smi", "gpus": [{"index","name","free_mb","total_mb","used_mb","util_pct","busy","uuid","processes"}...]}.
endpoints.bad_input: ?ssh_port=99x -> 400 "Invalid ssh_port". Malformed host -> 400.
endpoints.notes: Always 200, ok flag carries probe result. host= mode requires SSH creds. Probe timeouts 4-8s each; AMD sysfs path can issue several SSH round-trips.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch trending HuggingFace models from the public HF API, size-estimated and filtered by available VRAM
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/cookbook/hf-latest?vram_gb=24&limit=5&pipeline=text-generation with any logged-in session. Expect 200 {"models": [{"repo_id", "downloads", "likes", "createdAt", "tags", "pipeline_tag", "est_vram_gb", "needed_vram_gb"}...]} with <=5 entries whose needed_vram_gb <= 24. vram_gb=0 disables the size filter.
endpoints.bad_input: vram_gb=abc -> 422 (FastAPI float coercion).
endpoints.notes: Only endpoint in this module gated by require_user (not admin). Requires outbound HTTPS to huggingface.co/api/models (no credentials); network failure returns 200 {"models": [], "error": ...}. 15s httpx timeout.

endpoints.purpose: Send TERM/KILL/INT to a PID holding GPU memory, locally or over SSH
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: start a throwaway process (e.g. `sleep 600 &`, note its PID >=100). POST /api/cookbook/kill-pid with JSON {"pid": <that pid>, "signal": "TERM"}. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "pid": <pid>, "signal": "TERM"}. Verify the sleep process is gone. Dead/nonexistent PID returns 200 {"ok": false, "error": "..."}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"pid": 50} -> 400 "Refusing to signal PID 50 (<100, likely system process)". {"pid": 5000, "signal": "HUP"} -> 400 "signal must be TERM, KILL, or INT".
endpoints.notes: CAUTION: kills real processes owned by the server user — only test against a fixture process you started. Not classed DESTRUCTIVE (single-target, guarded) but treat carefully. host= mode needs SSH.

endpoints.purpose: SSH into a remote server and install Cookbook prerequisites (tmux, python, huggingface_hub), with Windows/Termux/Linux detection
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/cookbook/setup with JSON {"host": "user@gpu-box", "ssh_port": "22"}. Needs working passwordless SSH (Cookbook key in remote authorized_keys). Expect 200 {"ok": true, "output": "...OK", "platform": "linux"|"termux"|"windows"}. Without reachable host expect 200 {"ok": false, ...} after SSH failure or {"ok": false, "error": "Setup timed out (120s)"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"host": ""} -> 400 "host is required". {"host": "x", "ssh_port": "abc"} -> 400 "Invalid ssh_port".
endpoints.notes: Untestable happy-path without a remote SSH target; runs apt/pacman/dnf/pip installs ON the remote (mutating). Up to ~140s wall time (2x10s detection + 120s setup). Without a real host it hangs for SSH connect timeouts before returning ok:false.

endpoints.purpose: Return whether the Cookbook SSH public key exists and its contents
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/cookbook/ssh-key with admin session cookie. No params. Expect 200 with {"configured": bool, "public_key": "ssh-ed25519 ..." or ""}. Works even when no key exists (configured=false, public_key="").
endpoints.bad_input: Call without admin session -> 403 from require_admin (401 from middleware if no session at all).
endpoints.notes: Reads ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (or /app/.ssh inside Docker). Read-only, no fixtures.

endpoints.purpose: Generate the Cookbook ed25519 SSH keypair if missing and return the public key
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/cookbook/ssh-key with empty body, admin session. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "public_key": "ssh-ed25519 ... odysseus-cookbook"}. Idempotent: if key already exists it just re-chmods and returns it.
endpoints.bad_input: Without admin session -> 403.
endpoints.notes: SIDE EFFECT: creates ~/.ssh (or /app/.ssh) dir and writes id_ed25519/id_ed25519.pub via ssh-keygen subprocess. On failure returns 200 {"ok": false, "error": ...}. Safe to run on a test box but it writes a real key into the user's ~/.ssh if one is absent.

endpoints.purpose: Load the persisted cookbook state JSON (tasks, servers, presets, settings) with HF token masked
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/cookbook/state with admin session. Expect 200 with the state dict, or {} when data/cookbook_state.json is absent/corrupt. If env.hfToken is stored, response replaces it with hfTokenConfigured (bool) and hfTokenMasked (e.g. "hf_a...wxyz") — raw token must never appear.
endpoints.bad_input: No admin session -> 403/401.
endpoints.notes: Reads $DATA_DIR/cookbook_state.json (DATA_DIR env, default ./data). Pure read.

endpoints.purpose: Persist cookbook state for cross-device sync, with anti-wipe merge guards for env.servers and recent tasks, encrypting hfToken at rest
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/cookbook/state with JSON body like {"tasks": [{"sessionId": "serve-test0001", "type": "serve", "name": "test", "ts": <now ms>}], "env": {"servers": []}}. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "preserved": 0}. Round-trip: GET /api/cookbook/state should return what was written. Merge guard: on-disk tasks added <60s ago that are missing from the body are re-appended (preserved count > 0).
endpoints.bad_input: Non-dict JSON body (e.g. "[]") is coerced to {} and still returns {"ok": true} — no 4xx; errors surface as 200 {"ok": false, "error": ...}.
endpoints.notes: Writes data/cookbook_state.json atomically. If body contains env.hfToken it is validated then encrypted via src.secret_storage; empty incoming token preserves the on-disk one. Empty incoming env.servers never clobbers populated on-disk servers. This file feeds /api/cookbook/tasks/status, so it's the fixture-setter for that endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Poll liveness/progress/diagnosis of every cookbook tmux (or detached) download/serve session saved in cookbook state
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: save at least one task via POST /api/cookbook/state with tasks=[{"sessionId": "cookbook-deadbeef", "type": "download", "repoId": "x/y", "ts": <now ms>}]. GET /api/cookbook/tasks/status -> 200 {"tasks": [{"session_id": "cookbook-deadbeef", "type": "download", "model": "y", "status": "stopped" (no such tmux session), "progress", "phase", "diagnosis", "output_tail", "cmd", "tps", "reqs", "pct", "remote": "local"}]}. With no saved tasks expect {"tasks": []}.
endpoints.bad_input: Tasks with unsafe sessionId/remoteHost/sshPort in state are silently skipped (logged), not errored.
endpoints.notes: Runs `tmux has-session`/`capture-pane` subprocesses (10s timeout each) per task in a worker thread; remote tasks SSH out per poll. Serve tasks get _parse_serve_phase + _diagnose_serve_output structured diagnosis. Depends entirely on cookbook_state.json as fixture.

endpoints.purpose: Clear the custom embedding endpoint and revert the app to local fastembed
endpoints.test_plan: DELETE /api/embeddings/endpoint with admin session. Expect 200 {"success": true} (idempotent — succeeds even when nothing is configured). Verify GET /api/embeddings/endpoint returns active=false afterwards.
endpoints.bad_input: No admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: SIDE EFFECTS: deletes data/embedding_endpoint.json, pops EMBEDDING_URL/EMBEDDING_MODEL env vars, resets RAG singleton and ChromaDB client. Good cleanup step after POST /api/embeddings/endpoint tests.

endpoints.purpose: Get the configured custom HTTP embedding endpoint (URL/model/active flag)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/embeddings/endpoint. Expect 200 {"url": "" (or saved/EMBEDDING_URL value), "model": "", "active": false} on a fresh install; active=true when a URL is saved or EMBEDDING_URL env is set.
endpoints.bad_input: No admin -> 403.
endpoints.notes: Reads data/embedding_endpoint.json plus EMBEDDING_URL/EMBEDDING_MODEL env.

endpoints.purpose: Save a custom OpenAI-style embedding endpoint URL after a live health check, and hot-swap the app's RAG/Chroma embedding stack onto it
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: run a stub HTTP server that returns 200 to POST {"input": ["test"], "model": "test"} (e.g. python http.server wrapper on 127.0.0.1:9999). POST /api/embeddings/endpoint as form data: url=http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1/embeddings&model=test-model (Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded). Expect 200 {"success": true, "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1/embeddings", "model": "test-model"}. Verify GET /api/embeddings/endpoint now shows active=true. Clean up with DELETE /api/embeddings/endpoint.
endpoints.bad_input: url= (empty) -> 400 "URL is required". Unreachable URL like http://127.0.0.1:1/x -> 400 "Endpoint unreachable: ...". Missing url field entirely -> 422.
endpoints.notes: FORM body, not JSON. SIDE EFFECTS: performs an outbound httpx POST health check (10s timeout); writes data/embedding_endpoint.json; sets EMBEDDING_URL/EMBEDDING_MODEL process env; resets the RAG singleton, HTTP-embed down-latch, and ChromaDB client — affects embeddings app-wide. Always pair with DELETE in tests.

endpoints.purpose: List all fastembed-supported embedding models with downloaded/downloading/active/recommended flags and cached size
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/embeddings/models with admin session. Expect 200 JSON array of {"model", "dim", "size_gb", "description", "downloaded", "downloading", "active", "recommended", "cached_size_mb"}, sorted active-first. Exactly one entry should have active=true (default sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 unless FASTEMBED_MODEL is set).
endpoints.bad_input: No admin -> 403. If fastembed not installed -> 503 "fastembed is not installed".
endpoints.notes: Router-level Depends(require_admin) covers all /api/embeddings/* routes. Walks the fastembed cache dir (FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH env, default data/fastembed_cache) to compute sizes.

endpoints.purpose: Delete a cached (non-active) embedding model from the fastembed cache directory
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: first download a small non-active model (e.g. BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, assuming the active model is the default all-MiniLM-L6-v2). DELETE /api/embeddings/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 -> 200 {"deleted": true, "model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"}. Deleting a known-but-uncached model -> 200 {"deleted": false, "message": "Model not cached"}.
endpoints.bad_input: DELETE the active model (sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by default) -> 400 "Cannot delete the active embedding model". Unknown model -> 404. Currently-downloading model -> 400.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD (shutil.rmtree of one cache dir), not classed DESTRUCTIVE. Removes real cached files — re-download needed afterwards.

endpoints.purpose: Report downloaded/downloading state for one fastembed model
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/embeddings/models/BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5/status. Expect 200 {"model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5", "downloaded": bool, "downloading": bool}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown model name in path -> 404 "Unknown model: ...".
endpoints.notes: 503 if fastembed not installed. Cheap polling companion to the download endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Rank image-generation (diffusion) models against detected or simulated hardware (single-GPU VRAM basis)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/hwfit/image-models?manual_mode=gpu&manual_vram_gb=24&sort=fit. Expect 200 {"system": {... "gpu_vram_gb": 24, "gpu_count": 1 ...}, "models": [ranked image models]}. Plain GET works on real hardware; on a no-GPU box gpu_count becomes 0 and CPU-fit results return.
endpoints.bad_input: fresh=xyz -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Same no-endpoint-auth caveat as /api/hwfit/system. Forces single-GPU math (max per-GPU VRAM). Uses services.hwfit.image_models.rank_image_models.

endpoints.purpose: Rank LLM models from the bundled catalog against detected (or simulated) hardware and return scored fit results
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/hwfit/models?limit=5&manual_mode=gpu&manual_gpu_count=1&manual_vram_gb=24&manual_backend=cuda. Expect 200 {"system": {... "manual_hardware": true, "gpu_vram_gb": 24 ...}, "models": [<=5 scored entries]}. Plain GET /api/hwfit/models also works against real local hardware. If the catalog file is missing, 200 {"system":..., "models": [], "error": "Model catalog missing or empty: <path>"}.
endpoints.bad_input: ?gpu_count=abc -> 500 (unhandled ValueError: int(gpu_count) at line 151 has no try/except, unlike gpu_group). ?limit=abc -> 422.
endpoints.notes: manual_mode in {gpu, ram} replaces detected hardware entirely (simulator). gpu_count=0 forces RAM-only ranking; gpu_group selects a homogeneous GPU pool. Depends on services.hwfit catalog (models.get_models) and hardware detection cache; host= variant needs SSH. ignore_detected_gpu/ignore_detected_ram zero out detection.

endpoints.purpose: Detect and return current system hardware (CPU/RAM/GPU/backend), local or remote via SSH, with per-host caching
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/hwfit/system with a logged-in session, no params. Expect 200 JSON with detected fields (e.g. has_gpu, gpu_vram_gb, gpu_count, total_ram_gb, available_ram_gb, backend, gpus, gpu_groups). Add ?fresh=true to bypass the per-host detection cache. ?host=user@server runs detection over SSH (needs creds).
endpoints.bad_input: fresh=notabool -> 422.
endpoints.notes: No endpoint-level auth check — protected only by the global AuthMiddleware (any session; open on localhost when LOCALHOST_BYPASS or AUTH_ENABLED=false). Delegates to services.hwfit.hardware.detect_system.

endpoints.purpose: Scan the HF cache (plus optional comma-separated model dirs) for cached models, locally or over SSH
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/model/cached (no params) with admin session. Expect 200 {"models": [{"repo_id", "size", "nb_files", "has_incomplete", "status": "ready"|"downloading", "path", "is_diffusion"}...], "host": "local"}. Empty cache yields {"models": [], "host": "local"}. Optional query: model_dir=/some/dir, host=user@server, ssh_port, platform.
endpoints.bad_input: ?ssh_port=abc -> 400 "Invalid ssh_port". Invalid host format -> 400 from _validate_remote_host.
endpoints.notes: Writes scan_cache.py into TMUX_LOG_DIR and runs it with the local python (or via ssh for host=). 60s subprocess timeout (asyncio.wait_for raises -> 500 on timeout). Local mode needs no external creds.

endpoints.purpose: List the caller's past comparisons (newest first, max 50)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: at least one comparison via /api/compare/record. GET /api/compare/history. Expect 200 JSON array of {id, prompt (truncated to 100 chars), model_a, model_b, winner, is_blind, voted_at, created_at}.
endpoints.notes: Owner-filtered only when user is set; in no-auth mode returns everyone's.

endpoints.purpose: Lightweight one-shot endpoint to record a finished comparison vote from the frontend (no sessions created)
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/compare/record with JSON {"prompt": "What is 2+2?", "models": ["llama3", "mistral"], "winner": "llama3", "is_blind": true}. Expect 200 {"status": "ok", "id": "<uuid>"}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing required field (e.g. no winner) -> 422 (pydantic RecordVoteRequest).
endpoints.notes: JSON body (unlike /start and /vote which are form-encoded). prompt truncated to 500 chars; >2 models stored as JSON in blind_mapping; winner is free-form (model name or 'tie' — not validated).

endpoints.purpose: Start a model A/B comparison: creates two ephemeral [CMP] chat sessions and a Comparison record with optional blind left/right mapping
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/compare/start as FORM data (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): prompt='What is 2+2?' model_a='llama3' model_b='mistral' endpoint_a='http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1' endpoint_b='http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1' is_blind='true'. Expect 200 {id, session_left, session_right, model_left, model_right, is_blind:true, mapping:{left,right}}. The endpoints need not be live for this call itself.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing any required form field (e.g. no model_b) -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded, not JSON. Side effects: creates TWO persistent sessions named '[CMP] <model>' (pollute the session list until deleted) and one Comparison row. Copies the API key from any ModelEndpoint row matching the endpoint base URL into the session headers. No LLM call happens here — the client streams via /api/chat_stream afterwards. Blind mapping randomly shuffles left/right.

endpoints.purpose: Hard-delete one comparison record
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: comparison from /api/compare/record. DELETE /api/compare/<comp_id>. Expect 200 {"status": "deleted"}; subsequent GET history no longer lists it.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown or unowned comp_id -> 404 'Comparison not found'.
endpoints.notes: Despite the docstring ('and its ephemeral sessions'), the code only deletes the Comparison row — the two [CMP] sessions created by /start are NOT deleted and must be cleaned up via the sessions API.

endpoints.purpose: Record the user's vote on a comparison and reveal model identities
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: comparison from /api/compare/start (no vote yet). POST /api/compare/<comp_id>/vote as FORM data winner='left'. Expect 200 {winner:'a'|'b', model_a, model_b, revealed:{left:<model>, right:<model>}}.
endpoints.bad_input: winner='middle' -> 400 "winner must be 'left', 'right', or 'tie'"; voting twice -> 400 'Already voted'; unknown comp_id -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded. Strict ownership: another user's (or null-owner mismatched) comparison -> 404. winner='tie' stores 'tie' literally.

endpoints.purpose: Create a living document (optionally linked to a chat session) with version 1
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/document with JSON {"title": "Test Doc", "content": "# Test Doc\n\nSome markdown body text for testing.", "language": "markdown"} (session_id optional; omit for a library doc). Expect 200 with doc dict: id (uuid), title, language, current_content, version_count=1, is_active=true, archived=false, owner stamped. Requires can_use_documents privilege (granted by default).
endpoints.bad_input: POST {"session_id": "nonexistent-uuid", "content": "x"} -> 404 'Session not found'. Posting into another user's session -> 403.
endpoints.notes: If language omitted, it is sniffed from content; content that looks like an email (To:/Subject: headers) forces language='email'. Fires event_bus 'document_created' (may trigger event-driven scheduled tasks). If content contains a pdf_source marker pointing to an upload the caller does not own -> 400.

endpoints.purpose: Soft-delete one document (is_active=false)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned doc. DELETE /api/document/<doc_id>. Expect 200 {"status": "deleted", "id": "<doc_id>"}. Doc disappears from library but row remains (GET /api/document/<doc_id> still returns it with is_active=false).
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown doc_id -> 404 'Document not found'.
endpoints.notes: Ordinary single-item soft delete — recoverable at DB level. Inactive empty docs are later hard-purged by /api/documents/tidy.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch one document with full current content
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: doc created via POST /api/document. GET /api/document/<doc_id>. Expect 200 doc dict {id, session_id, title, language, current_content, version_count, is_active, archived, created_at, updated_at, source_email_* fields}.
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/document/nonexistent -> 404 'Document not found'. Another user's doc -> 404 (ownership hidden as not-found).
endpoints.notes: Ownership via _verify_doc_owner: trusts doc.owner column, legacy fallback to session owner; returns 404 (not 403) on ownership mismatch.

endpoints.purpose: Update document metadata only (title, language, session link)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned doc. PATCH /api/document/<doc_id> with JSON {"title": "Renamed Doc", "language": "python"}. Expect 200 doc dict with new title/language. Passing "session_id": "" unlinks the doc from its session (session_id -> null).
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown doc_id -> 404.
endpoints.notes: All fields optional; only provided fields change. No validation that a provided session_id exists or is owned by the caller.

endpoints.purpose: Replace document content (manual user edit); creates or coalesces a version
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned doc. PUT /api/document/<doc_id> with JSON {"content": "# Test Doc\n\nEdited body.", "summary": "manual edit"}. Expect 200 doc dict with current_content updated. NOTE: if the last user version is <60s old the edit coalesces in-place (version_count unchanged); wait 60s or check both behaviors. Identical content is a no-op returning the unchanged doc.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing required 'content' field -> 422 (pydantic DocumentUpdate). Unknown doc_id -> 404.
endpoints.notes: VERSION_COALESCE_SECONDS=60 — back-to-back saves within 60s update the latest 'user' version in place. Content with a pdf_source marker for an unowned upload -> 400.

endpoints.purpose: Soft-archive or restore a document (archived flag only)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned doc. POST /api/document/<doc_id>/archive?archived=true (no body). Expect 200 {ok:true, id:<doc_id>, archived:true}. Then POST ...?archived=false to restore and verify archived:false.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown doc_id -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Query param archived defaults to true. Archived docs disappear from default library view, appear with ?archived=true.

endpoints.purpose: Download the filled PDF (form values + signature stamps + annotations burned in)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: PDF-backed doc. GET /api/document/<doc_id>/export-pdf. Expect 200, Content-Type application/pdf, Content-Disposition attachment with filename '<slugged-title>_annotated.pdf', valid PDF bytes.
