endpoints.bad_input: Non-PDF doc -> 400 'Document is not linked to a source PDF'; unknown doc -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Splits markdown values into text fields (fill_fields) vs signature fields (stamp_signatures, ids 'signature:<id>' resolved owner-filtered). stamp failures are logged but non-fatal (falls back to less-stamped output).

endpoints.purpose: Return the field->value mapping that would be written into the source PDF form (confirmation-modal data)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a FORM PDF imported via /api/documents/import-pdf (AcroForm PDF, which creates the field sidecar). POST /api/document/<doc_id>/export-pdf/preview, empty body. Expect 200 {doc_id, upload_id, fields:[{name,label,type,options,page,value}], unknown_fields:[], total:int, filled:int}.
endpoints.bad_input: Run against a plain markdown doc -> 400 'Document is not linked to a source PDF'. Plain (non-form) PDF doc -> 404 'Field schema sidecar missing for source PDF'.
endpoints.notes: Requires the .fields sidecar JSON saved at import time next to the upload.

endpoints.purpose: Re-run pypdf(+VL OCR) text extraction on the doc's source PDF and replace the doc body with the result; bumps a new 'ocr' version
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a doc created via /api/documents/import-pdf (must contain a pdf_source marker referencing an upload the caller owns). POST /api/document/<doc_id>/extract-pdf-text with empty body. Expect 200 {ok:true, id, extracted:true, chars:int} (or extracted:false with reason 'No readable content' for unreadable PDFs). Side effect: doc content rewritten below the title, version_count+1, new DocumentVersion source='ocr'.
endpoints.bad_input: Run against a plain markdown doc (no pdf_source marker) -> 400 'Document is not a PDF — no pdf_source marker found'.
endpoints.notes: Idempotent on content layout. VL OCR LLM call only fires for image-heavy/low-text pages — text PDFs are pure pypdf (no LLM). Not timeout-exempt: scanned multi-page PDFs can hit the 45s global 504.

endpoints.purpose: Render one page of the doc's source PDF as a PNG image (2x scale, no values stamped)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: PDF-backed doc. GET /api/document/<doc_id>/page/1.png. Expect 200, Content-Type image/png, Cache-Control 'public, max-age=3600', valid PNG bytes.
endpoints.bad_input: GET .../page/9999.png -> 404 'Page out of range'; page 0 -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Requires PyMuPDF (503 if unavailable). page_no is 1-based.

endpoints.purpose: Flatten the filled/signed PDF, stage it in the email compose dir, and return reply headers (To/Subject/In-Reply-To) for the source email
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture chain: doc must have been created from an email attachment (via /api/email/attachment-as-doc) so source_email_uid/source_email_folder are set, plus a working IMAP account. POST /api/document/<doc_id>/prepare-signed-reply, empty body. Expect 200 {ok:true, attachment:{token:'<uuid>_<name>_signed.pdf', filename, size}, reply:{to, to_name, subject:'Re: ...', in_reply_to, references, account_id, source_uid, source_folder, source_message_id}}.
endpoints.bad_input: Any doc without source_email_* metadata -> 400 'Document has no source email — cannot reply'; doc without pdf_source marker -> 400.
endpoints.notes: Requires IMAP credentials (header fetch is best-effort: on IMAP failure it still returns 200 with empty to/subject, falling back to stored message-id). Writes the flattened PDF into ODYSSEUS_MAIL_ATTACHMENTS_DIR/_compose (default data/mail-attachments/_compose) using the '<uuid>_<filename>' token format /api/email/send expects. Hard to test happy-path without the email pipeline; the 400s are cheap to verify.

endpoints.purpose: Per-page metadata for the interactive PDF view: image dimensions + form-field rects in pixel coords
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: PDF-backed doc (import-pdf). GET /api/document/<doc_id>/render-pages. Expect 200 {doc_id, scale:2.0, pages:[{page:1, width:int, height:int, fields:[{name,type,label,options,value,rect_px:[x0,y0,x1,y1]}]}]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-PDF doc -> 400 'Document is not linked to a source PDF'.
endpoints.notes: Requires PyMuPDF (fitz) loadable via load_pymupdf_for_pdf_viewer — returns 503 with explanation if unavailable. fields list empty for non-form PDFs.

endpoints.purpose: Inline PDF preview: source PDF filled with current markdown form values + freeform annotations stamped
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: PDF-backed doc. GET /api/document/<doc_id>/render-pdf. Expect 200, Content-Type application/pdf, Content-Disposition: inline, valid PDF bytes. Temp files cleaned post-send via BackgroundTask.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-PDF doc -> 400 'Document is not linked to a source PDF'.

endpoints.bad_input: Unknown doc_id -> 200 [] (ownership check only runs when the doc exists — empty list, not 404).

endpoints.purpose: Bundle selected documents into a downloadable .zip (one text file per doc, extension by language)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: 1-2 owned docs. POST /api/documents/export-zip with JSON {"ids": ["<doc_id1>", "<doc_id2>"]}. Expect 200, Content-Type application/zip, Content-Disposition attachment filename=documents.zip; zip contains one file per owned doc (e.g. Test_Doc.md).
endpoints.bad_input: Body {} or {"ids": []} -> 400 'No documents specified'. All-unowned/unknown ids -> 404 'No documents found'.

endpoints.purpose: Upload a PDF (multipart) and create a Document from it — form-backed markdown if AcroForm fields exist, else plain PDF doc with pdf_source marker
endpoints.test_plan: curl -X POST /api/documents/import-pdf -F 'file=@sample.pdf' (optional -F 'session_id=<owned-session-uuid>'). Needs a real PDF file fixture. Expect 200 with doc dict (id, title from filename, current_content containing a pdf_source/upload marker, version_count>=1). Requires can_use_documents privilege and a configured upload_handler.
endpoints.bad_input: session_id of a nonexistent session -> 404 'Session not found'; missing file field -> 422.

Text extraction uses pypdf; pages with images and <50 chars of text trigger a vision-LLM OCR call (analyze_image_with_vl) — a plain text PDF makes no LLM call, a scanned PDF does. Subject to the global 45s REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT? No — path starts with /api/upload exemption does NOT apply; /api/documents/import-pdf is NOT timeout-exempt, so big scanned PDFs may 504.

endpoints.purpose: Paginated, searchable, owner-filtered document library with language facet counts
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/documents/library?sort=recent&offset=0&limit=20 (optional search=hello&language=markdown&archived=false). Fixture: at least one doc created via POST /api/document. endpoints.purpose: List all documents belonging to one chat session (newest first)

GET /api/email/list?folder=INBOX&limit=10&offset=0&filter=all -> 200 {"emails":[{uid,message_id,subject,from_name,from_address,to,cc,date,is_read,is_answered,is_flagged,has_attachments,tags,...}],"total":N,"folder":"INBOX","offset":0}. endpoints.purpose: User override: clear spam verdict (spam_verdict=0) for a UID in the email_tags SQLite table
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/email/12345/unflag-spam (no body) -> 200 {"ok":true}. Works even if uid has no row (UPDATE matches nothing). No IMAP needed — pure SQLite write to data/scheduled_emails.db.
endpoints.bad_input: None obvious — any uid string returns {"ok":true}.
endpoints.notes: Updates all email_tags rows with that uid regardless of owner/folder.

endpoints.purpose: List untagged image ids queued for client-driven AI tagging (does NOT itself call a model)
endpoints.test_plan: curl -X POST '/api/gallery/ai-tag-batch?limit=10' → 200 {"ok": true, "queued": N, "total_untagged": N, "image_ids": [...]}. Optional album_id query param. Fixture: an owned image with empty ai_tags to get nonzero queued.
endpoints.notes: Pure DB read despite the name — the client then calls POST /api/gallery/{id}/ai-tag per id. limit clamped to 1..500.

endpoints.purpose: AI upscale via configured diffusion server's /v1/images/upscale
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: an enabled ModelEndpoint row with model_type='image', plus a diffusion server exposing /v1/images/upscale. multipart: curl -F 'image=@test.png' -F 'scale=2' /api/gallery/ai-upscale → 200 {"image": "<b64 png>"}. Without an image endpoint configured → 400 'No image generation endpoint configured...'.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'image' form field → 400 'No image'
endpoints.notes: Gated by require_privilege('can_generate_images') (401 if no session, 403 if privilege flag false; no-op in single-user/unconfigured mode). Upstream failures return HTTP 200 with {"error": ...} — check body. WARNING: /api/gallery/* is NOT exempt from the app-wide 45s REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT but the httpx call allows 120s, so slow upscales 504 at 45s.

endpoints.purpose: List the caller's albums with photo counts and cover URLs
endpoints.test_plan: curl -b cookie /api/gallery/albums → 200 {"albums": [{"id", "name", "description", "cover_url", "count", "created_at"}]}. Empty list ok with no fixtures.
endpoints.notes: cover_url points at /api/generated-image/<filename> (separate route). If user is falsy ('' single-user mode) returns ALL albums — owner filter is 'if user:'.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new album
endpoints.test_plan: curl -X POST -d '{"name": "Vacation 2026", "description": "Greece"}' /api/gallery/albums → 200 {"ok": true, "id": "<uuid>", "name": "Vacation 2026"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"name": ""} or {} → 400 'Album name required'
endpoints.notes: Owner set from session.

endpoints.purpose: Delete an album; images inside are unassigned (album_id→NULL), not deleted
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned album. curl -X DELETE /api/gallery/albums/<id> → 200 {"ok": true}. Verify member images still exist in library with album_id null.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id → 404 'Album not found'
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD; non-destructive to photos.

endpoints.purpose: Update album name/description/cover image
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned album (POST /api/gallery/albums first); for cover, an owned image. curl -X PUT -d '{"name": "Renamed", "description": "new", "cover_id": "<image id>"}' /api/gallery/albums/<album_id> → 200 {"ok": true}. cover_id of "" clears the cover.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown/unowned album_id → 404 'Album not found'; cover_id referencing unowned image → 404 'Image not found'
endpoints.notes: All fields optional; only provided keys updated.

endpoints.purpose: Assign a set of owned images to an album
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned album + owned image(s). curl -X POST -d '{"image_ids": ["<img1>", "<img2>"]}' /api/gallery/albums/<album_id>/add → 200 {"ok": true, "count": 2}. Note count echoes the number of ids SENT, not rows actually updated.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown album → 404 'Album not found'
endpoints.notes: Only updates images the caller owns; unowned ids are silently skipped but still counted in 'count'.

endpoints.purpose: Remove a set of images from an album (album_id→NULL)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: album with member images. curl -X POST -d '{"image_ids": ["<img1>"]}' /api/gallery/albums/<album_id>/remove → 200 {"ok": true}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown album → 404 'Album not found'
endpoints.notes: Only affects rows whose album_id matches and (when user set) owned by caller.

endpoints.purpose: One-shot cleanup: remove user tags that duplicate ai_tags (case-insensitive) across all caller's images
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: image with tags='dog, beach' and ai_tags='dog'. curl -X POST /api/gallery/dedupe-tags → 200 {"ok": true, "rows_touched": 1, "tags_removed": 1}; image tags become 'beach'. With no overlap → rows_touched 0.
endpoints.notes: Bulk mutation but only removes redundant duplicates; idempotent (second call → 0/0).

endpoints.purpose: Bundle selected owned images into one zip download
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: 1+ owned images whose files exist on disk. curl -b cookie -X POST -d '{"ids": ["<id1>", "<id2>"]}' /api/gallery/download-zip -o out.zip → 200, Content-Type application/zip, Content-Disposition attachment; filename="gallery-photos.zip"; zip entries named from prompt (sanitized, deduped with -1/-2 suffixes).
endpoints.bad_input: {"ids": []} or no body → 400 'No images specified'; ids that match nothing → 404 'No images found'
endpoints.notes: Explicit 401 'Not authenticated' if no session user (one of the few handlers that checks). 404 'No image files found on disk' if rows exist but files missing.

endpoints.purpose: Paginated gallery browse with search/tag/model/album/favorites filters and recent/oldest/seeded-shuffle sort
endpoints.test_plan: curl -b cookie '/api/gallery/library?offset=0&limit=24&sort=recent' → 200 {"items": [...image dicts with id/filename/url/prompt/tags/ai_tags/favorite/width/height...], "total": N, "total_tagged": N, "tags": [...], "models": [...]}. Also test '?sort=shuffle&seed=42' (stable pagination), '?favorites=true', '?tag=a,b' (AND-stacked), '?search=dog'.
endpoints.bad_input: '?limit=0' or '?limit=101' → 422 (Query ge=1 le=100); '?offset=-1' → 422
endpoints.notes: Owner-scoped; items joined to session name. Returns 500 with detail on internal errors.

endpoints.purpose: Gallery summary stats: photo count, total bytes, favorites, album count
endpoints.test_plan: curl -b cookie /api/gallery/stats → 200 {"total_photos": N, "total_size": bytes, "total_size_human": "X.X MB", "favorites": N, "albums": N}. Works with zero fixtures (zeros).
endpoints.notes: Owner-scoped when user set.

endpoints.purpose: Style transfer via img2img on configured diffusion server (/v1/images/generations)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: enabled image ModelEndpoint + diffusion server. multipart: curl -F 'image=@test.png' -F 'prompt=van gogh style' -F 'strength=0.55' /api/gallery/style-transfer → 200 {"image": "<b64>"}. No endpoint → 400 'No image generation endpoint configured.'.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'image' field → 400 'No image'
endpoints.notes: require_privilege('can_generate_images'). Returns 200 {"error": ...} on upstream non-200 or exceptions. httpx timeout 180s but app middleware caps /api/gallery at 45s.

endpoints.purpose: Return distinct user tags across the caller's active gallery images
endpoints.test_plan: curl -b cookie /api/gallery/tags → 200 {"tags": ["beach", "dog", ...]} (sorted; [] when none). No fixture strictly required.
endpoints.notes: _owner_filter returns empty set when current_user is None (e.g. unauthenticated single-user edge).

endpoints.purpose: Upload an image/video file to the gallery with SHA-256 dedup and EXIF extraction
endpoints.test_plan: multipart form: curl -b session-cookie -F 'file=@test.png' http://host/api/gallery/upload (optional -F 'album_id=<album uuid>'). Expect 200 {"ok": true, "filename": "<12hex>.png", "id": "<uuid>"}. Re-uploading identical bytes returns 200 {"ok": false, "duplicate": true, "id": ..., "filename": ...}. Fixture: none (creates its own row).
endpoints.bad_input: Upload a file with unsupported extension, e.g. -F 'file=@x.txt' → 400 'Unsupported file type: .txt'; missing file field → 400 'No file provided'
endpoints.notes: Writes file to data/generated_images/ (relative to server CWD). Allowed exts: png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif + videos mp4/mov/webm/mkv/m4v (videos skip EXIF). Dedup is scoped to the calling user. Response may include exif_warning. Owner stored from session user; useful as the fixture-creator for all other gallery tests.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one image: remove file from disk, soft-delete DB row, purge chat-history references
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image (upload one first). curl -b cookie -X DELETE /api/gallery/<id> → 200 {"status": "deleted", "id": "<id>"}. Verify GET /api/gallery/<id> afterward still 200 (row soft-deleted, is_active=false, not removed) but library no longer lists it and the file is gone from data/generated_images/.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown or unowned id → 404 'Image not found'
endpoints.notes: Big side effect: best-effort scan of ChatMessage.meta_data for the image id/filename — matching tool_events are stripped and orphaned assistant+preceding user messages are HARD-deleted from chat history. Ordinary delete-one CRUD, but don't run against sessions whose chat history you need.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch one gallery image's metadata dict
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image. curl -b cookie /api/gallery/<id> → 200 {"id", "filename", "url": "/api/generated-image/<fn>", "prompt", "tags", "ai_tags", "favorite", "width", "height", "created_at", ...}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown or other-user's id → 404 'Image not found' (ownership masked as 404)
endpoints.notes: Catch-all path — fixed GET routes (tags/library/albums/stats) are registered earlier so they win; e.g. GET /api/gallery/doesnotexist returns this handler's 404.

endpoints.purpose: Update tags / favorite / album assignment on an image
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image. curl -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"favorite": true, "tags": "beach, sunset"}' /api/gallery/<id> → 200 full image dict with favorite=true and tags='beach, sunset'. {"album_id": ""} clears album.
endpoints.bad_input: {"favorite": "yes"} → 422 pydantic validation (GalleryPatch: tags str|None, favorite bool|None, album_id str|None)
endpoints.notes: Tags written here are deduped against ai_tags (case-insensitive) — a tag already in ai_tags is silently dropped from user tags.

endpoints.purpose: Toggle favorite flag on an image
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image. curl -X POST /api/gallery/<id>/favorite (no body) → 200 {"ok": true, "favorite": true}; second call → {"favorite": false}. Toggle, not idempotent set.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown/unowned id → 404 'Image not found'

endpoints.purpose: Rename a gallery photo (stores new label in the prompt column)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image. curl -b cookie -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name": "Beach day"}' /api/gallery/<id>/rename → 200 {"ok": true, "name": "Beach day"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"name": ""} → 400 'Name cannot be empty'; name >500 chars → 400 'Name too long'
endpoints.notes: Ownership enforced (403 'Not your image' for others, 404 unknown id).

endpoints.purpose: Replace an existing gallery image's file on disk (editor save-over)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: image uploaded by same user. multipart: curl -b cookie -F 'image=@new.png' /api/gallery/<id>/replace → 200 {"ok": true, "width": W, "height": H}. File on disk is overwritten in place (same filename).
endpoints.bad_input: POST with no 'image' form field → 400 'No image provided'; nonexistent id → 404 'Image not found'; another user's image → 403 'Not your image'
endpoints.notes: Overwrites data/generated_images/<filename>. Width/height refreshed via PIL (best-effort). Note form field is 'image' here vs 'file' on /upload.

endpoints.purpose: Rotate image file on disk by 90/-90/180/270 degrees, update dims+hash in DB
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned image whose file exists on disk. curl -X POST -d '{"angle": 90}' /api/gallery/<id>/rotate → 200 {"ok": true, "width": <new W>, "height": <new H>} (W/H swapped for 90). File re-encoded (JPEG/WEBP q95 or PNG) and file_hash/file_size updated.
endpoints.bad_input: {"angle": 45} → 400 'Angle must be 90, -90, 180, or 270'; {"angle": "x"} → 400 'Invalid angle'
endpoints.notes: Destructive to file bytes (re-encode); 404 'Image file not found' if DB row exists but file missing on disk. Rotation is clockwise convention.

endpoints.purpose: Face enhancement: GFPGAN v1.4 if installed, else pure-PIL denoise/sharpen/contrast fallback
endpoints.test_plan: Body: {"image": "<b64 jpg/png>"} → 200 {"image": "<b64 PNG>"}; when GFPGAN absent the response also has "method": "pil" — fallback always works, making this safely testable without ML deps.
endpoints.bad_input: {} → 400 'No image provided'
endpoints.notes: require_privilege('can_generate_images'). GFPGAN path downloads GFPGANv1.4.pth from GitHub into tempdir and needs cv2 — long-running on first call; PIL path is fast. Other exceptions → 500 'Face enhancement failed: ...'.

endpoints.purpose: img2img harmonize (color match / seam fix) — tries /images/harmonize, /images/img2img, /images/variations, then A1111 /sdapi/v1/img2img
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: enabled image ModelEndpoint pointing at a diffusion server exposing one of the four routes. Body: {"image": "<b64>", "prompt": "natural lighting", "color_match": 0.45, "seam_fix": 0.2, "body_mask": "<b64>"} → 200 {"image": "<b64>"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {} (no image) → 400 'No image provided'; pointing _endpoint at api.openai.com → 400 'Harmonize needs a diffusion server...'
endpoints.notes: require_privilege('can_generate_images'). Explicitly refuses OpenAI. 502 if no candidate route works (message lists tried routes), 502 on ConnectError, 504 at 240s. Exempt from app 45s timeout. Legacy 'strength' maps to color_match.

endpoints.purpose: Proxy inpaint to self-hosted diffusion server, or reshape for OpenAI /v1/images/edits (alpha-mask conversion + composite-back)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: enabled image ModelEndpoint (diffusion server with /v1/images/inpaint) OR pass body '_endpoint'. Body: {"image": "<b64 png>", "mask": "<b64 png, white=regenerate>", "prompt": "red hat", "width": 1024, "height": 1024, "_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:7860", "_model": ""} → 200 {"image": "<b64>"} (OpenAI path) or the diffusion server's JSON passthrough. No endpoint configured and no _endpoint → 400 'No image generation endpoint configured...'.
endpoints.bad_input: With OpenAI endpoint and _model containing 'dall-e-3' → 400 "dall-e-3 doesn't support image edits..."; OpenAI endpoint with no stored api_key → 400
endpoints.notes: require_privilege('can_generate_images'). OpenAI path needs api_key stored on the ModelEndpoint row; converts SD mask convention to alpha, picks size 1024x1024/1024x1536/1536x1024, then composites result over source using the original mask. 504 on 120s timeout; 502 on upstream errors. /api/image/* is exempt from the 45s app hard-timeout.

endpoints.purpose: Local PIL unsharp-mask sharpening (no AI, no external deps)
endpoints.test_plan: Body: {"image": "<b64 of any png/jpg>", "amount": 50} → 200 {"image": "<b64 PNG>"}. No fixtures, no model endpoint needed — good smoke test for the /api/image group.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing/invalid image field → unhandled TypeError/binascii error → 500
endpoints.notes: NO require_privilege and no user lookup — only the global auth middleware gates it. amount defaults to 50 (percent).

endpoints.purpose: Report install status of optional packages (tmux, docker, vllm, sglang, llama_cpp, diffusers, hf_transfer, rembg, realesrgan, playwright) locally or on a remote server via SSH
endpoints.test_plan: Local happy path (no fixtures): GET /api/cookbook/packages with admin session. Expect 200 {"packages": [...]} where each item has name, pip, desc, category, target, installed (bool); docker row additionally has applicable + install_hint. Remote variant GET /api/cookbook/packages?host=user@gpu1&ssh_port=22&venv=~/venv requires working SSH key auth to that host (skip without creds; SSH failures degrade gracefully to installed:false rather than erroring).
endpoints.bad_input: ssh_port=abc (with host) -> 400 'Invalid ssh_port'; venv with shell metacharacters e.g. venv=$(id) -> 400 'invalid venv path'; request with header sec-fetch-site: cross-site -> 403 'Cross-site request rejected'
endpoints.notes: host param triggers outbound ssh with ConnectTimeout=6, StrictHostKeyChecking=no, 12s probe timeout — remote mode is EXTERNAL-CREDS in practice. host values starting with '-' rejected (400 'invalid ssh host'). Subject to the global 45s hard timeout but local path is fast.

endpoints.purpose: Return detailed database statistics (core.database.get_detailed_stats)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/db/stats with admin session. Expect 200 with a stats JSON object (table counts/sizes). No fixtures needed.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'
endpoints.notes: Any internal exception -> 500 'Failed to retrieve database statistics'.

endpoints.purpose: Localhost-only in-process tool execution proxy for per-agent Claude Code sessions (runs any Odysseus agent tool with full runtime state)
endpoints.test_plan: Must be called from 127.0.0.1 with NO proxy-forwarding headers and header X-Odysseus-Internal-Token: $ODYSSEUS_INTERNAL_TOKEN (set this env var before starting the app for a deterministic token; otherwise it's random per process). Optionally X-Odysseus-Owner: <existing username> for owner attribution. POST JSON {"tool": "bash", "args": {"command": "echo internal-ok"}}. Expect 200 {"ok": true, "result": <tool output containing 'internal-ok'>}. Unknown tool e.g. {"tool":"nope"} -> 200 {"ok": false, "error": "Unknown or invalid tool: nope"}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing/wrong X-Odysseus-Internal-Token (with valid admin cookie) -> 403 'forbidden'; non-JSON body -> 400 'invalid json body'; JSON without 'tool' -> 400 'tool required'
endpoints.notes: Double auth gate: AuthMiddleware in app.py validates token + trusted loopback (rejects if any of cf-connecting-ip/x-forwarded-for/etc. headers present) and sets current_user='internal-tool' or impersonated owner; the route re-checks the token (constant-time). Tool execution failures return 200 {ok:false,error}. Body also accepts session_id and workspace_root. Executes real tools (bash/python/web_search/email/MCP-namespaced mcp__server__tool) — pick harmless args.

endpoints.purpose: Start Google OAuth flow for an MCP server: redirect to Google (local access) or show paste-back HTML page (remote access)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: MCP server whose oauth_config JSON has keys_file pointing to an existing Google client-secrets JSON ({"installed":{"client_id":...,"client_secret":...}}) and a scopes list. GET /api/mcp/oauth/authorize/{id} with Host: localhost:7000 -> 307 redirect to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?... With non-localhost Host header -> 200 HTML paste-back page. Without real Google creds, only the error paths are testable: server without oauth_config -> 400 'Server has no OAuth config'.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown server_id -> 404; server with oauth_config but missing keys file on disk -> 400 'OAuth keys file not found'
endpoints.notes: Requires Google OAuth client-secrets file on disk (can be written via POST /api/mcp/servers oauth_file field). Redirect URI hardcoded to http://localhost:7000/api/mcp/oauth/callback. Behavior branches on Host header (localhost vs remote).

endpoints.purpose: Google OAuth callback — exchange auth code for tokens, save token file, connect the MCP server
endpoints.test_plan: Cannot complete happy path without a real Google authorization code. Smoke test the error path: GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback?code=fake&state=<existing_server_id_with_oauth_config> -> Google token exchange fails -> 400 HTML page 'Authorization Failed'. With state=<unknown_id> -> 404 HTML 'Server not found.' Responses are text/html, not JSON.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing code or state query params -> 422 validation error
endpoints.notes: Makes outbound POST to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. On success writes tokens to oauth_config.token_file path and spawns MCP server subprocess. All outcomes (success/failure) return HTML pages.

endpoints.purpose: Manual OAuth code exchange — user pastes the full callback URL copied from their browser (remote-device flow)
endpoints.test_plan: Happy path needs a real Google code. Testable smoke: POST form-encoded callback_url=http://localhost:7000/api/mcp/oauth/callback?code=fake to /api/mcp/oauth/exchange/{existing_oauth_server_id} -> Google rejects fake code -> 400 HTML 'Authorization Failed'. Returns HTML in all cases.
endpoints.bad_input: callback_url without a code= query param -> 400 HTML 'No authorization code found in the URL...'
endpoints.notes: Same Google token exchange + token-file write + server connect as the callback route. Missing callback_url form field -> 422.

endpoints.purpose: List all configured MCP servers with connection status, tool counts, and OAuth state
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/mcp/servers with admin session cookie. Expect 200 with JSON array (possibly empty); each entry has id, name, transport, command, args, env, url, is_enabled, status, tool_count, disabled_tool_count, enabled_tool_count, error, has_oauth, needs_oauth. Works with zero fixtures (empty list []).
endpoints.bad_input: No session cookie -> 401 from AuthMiddleware; non-admin user session -> 403 'Admin only'
endpoints.notes: Reads McpServer table + in-memory mcp_manager status. Built-in MCP servers may be registered at startup (register_builtin_servers) so list may be non-empty on fresh install.

endpoints.purpose: Register a new MCP server (stdio or SSE) and attempt connection; optionally writes Google OAuth client-credentials file
endpoints.test_plan: POST form-encoded: name=testsrv&transport=stdio&command=echo&args=["hi"]&env={}. Expect 200 with {id: <8-char uuid>, name: 'testsrv', connected: false (echo is not a real MCP server), status: 'error'|'disconnected', tool_count: 0, needs_oauth: false}. Endpoint succeeds (200) even when connection fails. Cleanup: DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id} afterwards.
endpoints.bad_input: transport=stdio with no command -> 400 'command is required for stdio transport'; transport=sse with no url -> 400 'url is required for SSE transport'
endpoints.notes: SIDE EFFECTS: inserts DB row, SPAWNS A SUBPROCESS for stdio transport (arbitrary binary execution — keep command harmless), and if oauth_file form field is valid JSON with dir/filename/client_id/client_secret it WRITES a credentials file to disk. Invalid JSON in args/env is silently coerced to []/{}. oauth_config with token_file that doesn't exist returns status 'needs_oauth' and skips connection.

endpoints.purpose: Disconnect and delete one MCP server config
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing server id (create a dummy first). DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id}. Expect 200 {"status": "deleted"}. Verify it's gone via GET /api/mcp/servers.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown server_id -> 404 'Server not found'
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD, not danger-zone. Useful as cleanup step for the add-server tests.

endpoints.purpose: Enable or disable an MCP server (connects/disconnects accordingly)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing server id. PATCH form-encoded body: is_enabled=false. Expect 200 {id: <server_id>, is_enabled: false}. Then is_enabled=true to re-enable (triggers connection attempt). Any string other than 'true' (case-insensitive) is treated as false.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing is_enabled form field -> 422 validation error; unknown server_id -> 404 'Server not found'
endpoints.notes: CORS config in app.py does not allow PATCH method cross-origin (allow_methods lacks PATCH) — irrelevant for curl, matters for browser-based testing from another origin. Enabling spawns subprocess.

endpoints.purpose: Disconnect and reconnect an existing MCP server
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a server via POST /api/mcp/servers first and capture its id. POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/reconnect (no body). Expect 200 with {connected: bool, status: str, tool_count: int, error: str|null}. connected:false with an error string is still a 200 happy-path for a dummy command.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown server_id -> 404 'Server not found'
endpoints.notes: Spawns subprocess for stdio servers. Safe to call repeatedly.

endpoints.purpose: List tools for a specific MCP server with per-tool is_disabled flag
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing server id. GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/tools. Expect 200 with array (empty [] for a dummy/disconnected server is a valid happy path); each item has name, server_id, is_disabled.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown server_id -> 404 'Server not found'
endpoints.notes: Returns [] rather than error when server exists but has no connected tools.

endpoints.purpose: Bulk-set the disabled-tools list for a server
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing server id. PATCH with JSON body {"disabled": ["some_tool"]}. Expect 200 {id: <server_id>, disabled_count: 1}. Send {"disabled": []} to clear (disabled_count: 0, column set to NULL).
endpoints.bad_input: {"disabled": "not-a-list"} -> 400 'disabled must be a list of tool names'
endpoints.notes: Tool names are NOT validated against actual tools — any strings accepted. Same CORS PATCH caveat as above.

endpoints.purpose: List all discovered MCP tools across all connected servers (respecting per-server disabled lists)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/mcp/tools with admin session. Expect 200 with JSON array (may be empty if no servers connected). Entries include name and server_id fields.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'
endpoints.notes: No fixtures strictly required; built-in MCP servers registered at startup may populate this.

endpoints.purpose: Return vector-RAG (ChromaDB) statistics, or an error payload if RAG unavailable
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/rag/stats with admin session. Expect 200. If ChromaDB is reachable: rag_manager.get_stats() dict. If not: 200 {"error": "RAG system not available"} — both are valid outcomes; record which.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session -> 403 'Admin only'
endpoints.notes: rag_available is computed once at app startup (src.rag_singleton.get_rag_manager); restarting ChromaDB after app boot won't flip this endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Execute a shell command on the host (cwd=$HOME) and return stdout/stderr/exit_code; 30s timeout
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"command": "echo hello"} with admin session. Expect 200 {"stdout": "hello\n", "stderr": "", "exit_code": 0}. Failing command e.g. {"command": "false"} -> 200 with exit_code 1. Empty/whitespace command -> 200 {"stdout":"","stderr":"No command provided","exit_code":1}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing 'command' field -> 422; non-admin or api-token ('api') user -> 403 'Admin only'
endpoints.notes: Arbitrary RCE by design (admin-gated). Output truncated at 200,000 chars. Timeout hardcoded at EXEC_TIMEOUT=30s (request body 'timeout' field is ignored by this endpoint, only used by /stream); timeouts return 200 with exit_code -1 and stderr message. Also accepts user=='internal-tool' loopback marker. Custom _require_admin returns silently if no auth_manager on app.state.

endpoints.purpose: Execute a shell command streaming output line-by-line over SSE; optional PTY mode and tmux background mode
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"command": "echo one; echo two", "timeout": 30} with admin session, Accept: text/event-stream. Expect 200 text/event-stream with events like data: {"stream":"stdout","data":"one"} ... terminated by data: {"exit_code": 0}. PTY variant: add "use_pty": true (POSIX only). tmux variant: {"command":"echo bg","use_tmux":true} -> first event announces 'Started tmux session: cookbook-xxxxxxxx', then output lines, then exit_code event.
endpoints.bad_input: Empty command -> 200 SSE with stderr event 'No command provided' then exit_code 1 (not an HTTP error)
endpoints.notes: SSE streaming; exempt from the global 45s REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT (prefix /api/shell/stream is whitelisted). Default timeout 120s; timeout:0 = run until client disconnects. tmux mode requires tmux binary, survives disconnect (background job semantics), writes wrapper script + log under $TMPDIR/odysseus-tmux/ (log cleaned up on completion). use_pty on a platform without pty support yields error event with error:'pty_unsupported' and exit_code -1.

endpoints.purpose: Diagnostic: extract a YouTube video id and fetch its transcript
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/test/youtube?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ with admin session. Expect 200 with {video_id: "dQw4w9WgXcQ", transcript_success: bool, transcript_length: int, transcript_preview: str, error: str|null}. transcript_success:false with an error is still 200 (YouTube may block/ratelimit server IPs) — treat 200 + well-formed shape as pass.
endpoints.bad_input: url=not-a-youtube-link -> 200 {"error": "Invalid YouTube URL"}; missing url query param -> 422
endpoints.notes: Requires outbound internet to YouTube; no credentials. All exceptions swallowed into 200 {error: str}. Subject to 45s hard timeout.

endpoints.purpose: List all memory entries for the current user
endpoints.test_plan: GET with session cookie. Expect 200 {"memory":[{id,text,category,owner,timestamp,...}]}. Empty list is valid for a fresh user.
endpoints.notes: Read-only. Useful to capture a memory_id for the /{memory_id} CRUD tests.

endpoints.purpose: Add a new memory entry (text + optional category/source/session_id)
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"text":"User prefers dark roast coffee","category":"preference","source":"user"}. Expect 200 {"ok":true,"count":N}. Re-posting identical text returns 200 {"ok":true,"count":N,"message":"Memory already exists"} (dedupe). Also accepts form-encoded fallback when no JSON body.
endpoints.bad_input: JSON {"text":" "} (whitespace only) -> 400 "empty memory"; {"text":""} -> 422 (pydantic min_length=1).
endpoints.notes: Gated by require_privilege(can_manage_memory) — 403 if the account's auth.json privilege flag is false (admins always pass; missing key defaults to allowed). Invalid category silently coerced to 'fact'. Side effects: persists to memory store, syncs vector index if memory_vector healthy, fires 'memory_added' event on event bus.

endpoints.purpose: List memories that were saved from a specific chat session
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a chat session via the session routes (capture its id), then POST /api/memory/add with {"text":"...","session_id":"<sid>"}. GET /api/memory/by-session/<sid> -> 200 {"session_id","session_name","memory_count","memories":[...]}.
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/memory/by-session/nonexistent-id -> 404 "Session ... not found".
endpoints.notes: 404 comes from session lookup, not memory lookup — requires the session to exist in session_manager.

endpoints.purpose: Debug which memories would be retrieved as relevant for a given query (relevance scoring dry-run)
endpoints.test_plan: POST form-encoded body `query=coffee` (Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded). Works with zero memories; for a meaningful result first create a memory via POST /api/memory/add with text mentioning coffee. Expect 200 with {"query":"coffee","total_memories":N,"relevant_count":M,"relevant_memories":[{"text":...,"category":...}]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Omit the `query` form field -> 422 validation error.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded, not JSON. Read-only. Scoped to current user's memories.

endpoints.purpose: Search memories by relevance with optional session_id/category filters
endpoints.test_plan: POST form-encoded `query=coffee&category=preference`. Fixture: a memory added via /api/memory/add containing 'coffee'. Expect 200 {"memories":[...],"total":N,"query":"coffee"} (max 20 items, threshold 0.05).
endpoints.bad_input: Missing `query` form field -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded. session_id/category filters apply before relevance ranking.

endpoints.purpose: Return all memories sorted newest-first with human timestamps and source session names
endpoints.test_plan: GET with session cookie. Expect 200 {"timeline":[{...,"timestamp_str":"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS","session_name":"..."}],"total":N}. Memories without timestamp/session show "Unknown".
endpoints.notes: Read-only; mutates returned dicts in memory only (adds timestamp_str/session_name).

endpoints.purpose: Delete one memory item by id
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a throwaway memory via /add, fetch its id. DELETE /api/memory/<id> -> 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Memory deleted successfully"}. Subsequent GET of the id -> 404.
endpoints.bad_input: DELETE unknown id -> 404 "Memory item ... not found".
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD (not DESTRUCTIVE class). Also removes the id from the vector index.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch a single memory item by id
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: memory created via /add; id from GET /api/memory. GET /api/memory/<id> -> 200 {"memory":{id,text,category,...}}.
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/memory/does-not-exist -> 404 "Memory not found".
endpoints.notes: Wildcard route declared last so literal subpaths (/timeline, /import, ...) win.

endpoints.purpose: Update a memory's text (and optionally category); refreshes timestamp
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing memory id. PUT form-encoded `text=Updated fact&category=fact` -> 200 {"ok":true,"message":"Memory updated successfully"}.
endpoints.bad_input: Missing `text` form field -> 422. Unknown id -> 404.
endpoints.notes: Form-encoded, not JSON. Side effect: vector index remove+re-add for the id when memory_vector is healthy. Ownership enforced (404 for other users' items).

endpoints.purpose: Pin or unpin a memory (pinned memories always included in chat context)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: add a memory, get its id from GET /api/memory. POST form-encoded `pinned=true` to /api/memory/<id>/pin -> 200 {"ok":true,"pinned":true}. `pinned=false` unpins.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Memory item ... not found". Another user's memory id -> 404 (ownership masked as not-found).
endpoints.notes: Declared before the /{memory_id} wildcard routes; ownership enforced via _verify_memory_owner.

endpoints.purpose: List the user's notes (active by default; archived/label filters)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/notes -> 200 {"notes":[...]} excluding archived, ordered pinned desc, sort_order asc, updated_at desc. GET /api/notes?archived=true lists archived newest-first. GET /api/notes?label=work filters by label.
endpoints.notes: SQLite-backed (Note table). Owner-scoped when auth configured.

endpoints.purpose: Create a note or checklist (Google Keep-style)
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"title":"Groceries","note_type":"checklist","items":[{"text":"Milk","done":false},{"text":"Eggs","done":false}],"color":"yellow","pinned":false} -> 200 full note dict with generated uuid "id", "owner", "created_at". Plain note: {"title":"Idea","content":"Build a birdhouse"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"items":"not-a-list"} -> 422 (items must be a list).
endpoints.notes: Optional fields: label, due_date (string), repeat (default "none"), image_url, source, session_id, sort_order. items stored as JSON string in DB.

endpoints.purpose: Dispatch a reminder for a note through the configured channel (browser/email/ntfy) with optional LLM synthesis line
endpoints.test_plan: POST JSON {"note_id":"<note uuid>","title":"Water plants","body":"Balcony plants need watering"} -> 200 {"synthesis":null|str,"email_sent":bool,"email_error":str,"ntfy_sent":bool,"ntfy_error":str,"browser_sent":bool}. With default settings (reminder_channel=browser, reminder_llm_synthesis=false) no LLM call and no email — safe to test. note_id can be any non-empty string (no DB lookup).
endpoints.bad_input: JSON without note_id -> 400 "note_id required". Anonymous call -> 401 "Not authenticated".
endpoints.notes: CAUTION when testing a live deployment: behavior depends on live settings — reminder_llm_synthesis=true triggers an LLM call (utility/default model), reminder_channel=email actually sends SMTP mail (per-owner email account config; recipient = reminder_email_to or from-address), reminder_channel=ntfy posts to the ntfy integration. Writes dedupe cache data/note_pings_<owner>.json; re-firing the same note_id within 25 min returns {skipped:true} for email/ntfy. queue_browser=False on this route so no in-app notification queued.

endpoints.purpose: Set sort_order for notes to match the given id order (drag-and-drop persistence)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: two notes with ids A and B. POST JSON {"ids":["B","A"]} -> 200 {"ok":true,"count":2}; subsequent GET /api/notes shows B before A (sort_order 0,1). Unknown ids are silently skipped but still counted in count.
endpoints.bad_input: {"ids":"not-a-list"} -> 400 "ids must be a list".
endpoints.notes: Owner-scoped; null-owner notes only reorderable when AuthManager is not configured (single-user mode).

endpoints.purpose: Delete one note
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: throwaway note created via POST /api/notes. DELETE /api/notes/<id> -> 200 {"ok":true}. GET afterwards -> 404.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Note not found".
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD, not DESTRUCTIVE class.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch a single note by id
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a note via POST /api/notes, capture id. GET /api/notes/<id> -> 200 note dict (id, title, content, items, pinned, archived, ai_classification, ...).
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Note not found"; other users' notes also 404 (ownership masked).
endpoints.notes: Strict ownership check (user is not None and note.owner != user -> 404).

endpoints.purpose: Partially update a note (only provided fields change)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: existing note id. PUT JSON {"title":"Groceries (updated)","pinned":true} -> 200 updated note dict. Updating items: {"items":[{"text":"Milk","done":true}]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Note not found".
endpoints.notes: All NoteUpdate fields optional: title, content, items, note_type, color, label, pinned, archived, due_date, image_url, repeat, sort_order, agent_session_id.

endpoints.purpose: Toggle a note's archived flag
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: active note. POST /api/notes/<id>/archive (empty body) -> 200 {"ok":true,"archived":true}; note then disappears from default GET /api/notes and appears under ?archived=true.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Note not found".
endpoints.notes: Toggle (no body).

endpoints.purpose: Toggle the done state of one checklist item by index
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: checklist note created with items=[{"text":"Milk","done":false}]. POST /api/notes/<id>/items/0/toggle -> 200 {"ok":true,"items":[{"text":"Milk","done":true}]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Index out of range (e.g. /items/99/toggle) -> 400 "Item index 99 out of range"; note with no items -> 400 "Note has no checklist items".
endpoints.notes: Index is path param int; negative or >= len(items) rejected.

endpoints.purpose: Toggle a note's pinned flag
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: note with pinned=false. POST /api/notes/<id>/pin (empty body) -> 200 {"ok":true,"pinned":true}; second call -> {"pinned":false}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown id -> 404 "Note not found".
endpoints.notes: Toggle (no body); ownership enforced.

endpoints.purpose: List indexed personal-docs files and tracked directories
endpoints.test_plan: GET with an admin session cookie -> 200 {"files":[{"name","size","path"}],"directories":[...]}. Empty arrays are valid on a fresh install.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin user session -> 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: Depends(require_user) + Depends(require_admin). require_admin also passes for internal-tool token or AUTH_ENABLED=false.

endpoints.purpose: Index a directory (recursively) into the ChromaDB RAG vector store
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create data/personal_docs/testdocs/ under the app root with a small .txt file; ChromaDB + embedding service must be reachable. POST JSON {"directory":"testdocs"} (relative paths resolve under data/personal_docs; absolute paths must stay inside it) -> 200 {"success":true,"message":"Successfully indexed N chunks from ...","indexed_count":N,"failed_count":0,"directory":"/abs/path"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"directory":"/etc"} -> 403 "Directory must be inside personal documents"; {"directory":"nope"} (missing dir) -> 404; empty/whitespace -> 422 (min_length=1) or 400.
endpoints.notes: Returns 503 "RAG system is not available" when ChromaDB is unreachable (lazy retry via get_rag_manager). Also registers the directory with personal_docs_manager. Embedding/indexing can be slow for large trees and is NOT timeout-exempt (45s -> 504 risk).

endpoints.purpose: Delete one file's chunks from the RAG index, delete it from disk if under uploads dir, and exclude it from listings
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a file uploaded via POST /api/personal/upload (get its stored path from GET /api/personal files[].path or data/personal_uploads/<owner>/<stem>-<hex>.txt). DELETE /api/personal/file?filepath=/abs/path/to/data/personal_uploads/<owner>/<file> -> 200 {"success":true,"removed_chunks":N,"deleted_from_disk":true}. Files outside the uploads dir return deleted_from_disk:false (index-only removal).
endpoints.bad_input: Omit `filepath` query param -> 422.
endpoints.notes: Disk deletion only inside data/personal_uploads (path-containment check). Exclusion persists across restarts via personal_docs_manager.exclude_file. RAG removal best-effort. Despite being a delete, it is ordinary single-item cleanup, admin-gated.

endpoints.purpose: Refresh the personal-docs file index from disk
endpoints.test_plan: POST with admin session, empty body -> 200 {"ok":true,"count":N} where N is the refreshed file count.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session -> 403 "Admin only".
endpoints.notes: Disk re-scan; duration scales with indexed directory size (45s global hard-timeout applies).

endpoints.purpose: Remove a directory from the RAG index and personal-docs tracking
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: directory previously added via /add_directory. DELETE /api/personal/remove_directory?directory=/abs/path/to/data/personal_docs/testdocs -> 200 {"success":true,"message":"Successfully removed ...","directory":"..."}. Succeeds (200) even for unknown directories — removal is best-effort.
endpoints.bad_input: Omit the `directory` query param -> 422.
endpoints.notes: RAG vector-store removal is best-effort (failures logged, still 200). No path containment check on removal.

endpoints.purpose: Upload one or more files (text/PDF) directly into the RAG index
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: ChromaDB/embedding service reachable. POST multipart with repeated `files` fields: curl -F 'files=@notes.txt' -F 'files=@paper.pdf' /api/personal/upload -> 200 {"success":true,"uploaded":["notes.txt","paper.pdf"],"indexed_count":N,"failed_count":0}. Files are stored under data/personal_uploads/<owner>/ with uuid-suffixed names and chunk-indexed (chunk_size 500).
endpoints.bad_input: No `files` field -> 422. (Oversized file > ODYSSEUS_PERSONAL_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES, default 25 MiB, is not an error — it is silently counted in failed_count.)
endpoints.notes: Only route in this module WITHOUT the admin gate — any logged-in user can use it (middleware-level auth still required). 503 "RAG system is not available — is the embedding service running?" without ChromaDB. Empty/undecodable files increment failed_count. Side effects: files written to disk, vectors added, uploads dir registered with personal_docs_manager.

endpoints.purpose: Resolve the caller's default chat endpoint+model (per-user prefs for regular users, global settings for admins, with fallback chain)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: logged-in session; for a non-empty result either be admin with settings.json default_endpoint_id set, or a user with prefs default_endpoint_id (PUT /api/prefs/default_endpoint_id {"value": "<ep_id>"}) pointing at an enabled endpoint they can see. GET /api/default-chat. Expect 200 {"endpoint_id": "<ep_id>", "endpoint_url": "http://.../chat/completions", "model": "<model-id>"}. With nothing configured: 200 {"endpoint_id": "", "endpoint_url": "", "model": ""}.
endpoints.notes: Owner-scoped: a user's default pointing at another user's endpoint resolves empty. Honors default_model_fallbacks list, then first enabled endpoint OWNED by the user (shared/null-owner excluded at this last-resort step). Empty model falls back to first cached model on the endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Scan the local network/host for model servers on common ports (Ollama, vLLM, etc.)
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. GET /api/discover. Expect 200 with model_discovery.discover_models() result (discovered host/port/model entries; empty-ish structure when nothing is running locally). Cheap to run when no local servers exist.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session: 403 Admin only.
endpoints.notes: Port scan can take several seconds when configured hosts are unreachable; subject to the 45s hard timeout. Read-only, no DB writes.

endpoints.purpose: Admin list of all ModelEndpoint rows with cached model lists, hidden counts, and online status
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + >=1 ModelEndpoint. GET /api/model-endpoints. Expect 200 JSON array: [{"id":...,"name":...,"base_url":...,"has_key":bool,"is_enabled":bool,"models":[...visible ids],"hidden_count":0,"online":bool,"status":"online"|"empty"|"offline","ping_error":null,"model_type":"llm","supports_tools":null|bool}]. Empty array when no endpoints exist.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session: 403 Admin only.
endpoints.notes: Uses cached_models (no live model probe), but enabled endpoints with NO cached models get a 1s live ping each — many dead endpoints slow this down. Path prefix /api/model-endpoints is exempt from the 45s hard timeout.

endpoints.purpose: Create (or dedupe-return existing) model endpoint; optionally probes for models; may auto-set global default chat endpoint
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/model-endpoints as form data (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1&name=test-ollama&skip_probe=true&shared=true. Expect 200 {"id": "<8-char uuid>", "name": "test-ollama", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1", "models": [], "online": false, "status": "offline"|"online"|"empty", "ping_error": ...}. Re-POST same base_url returns the existing row with "existing": true (dedupe). Cleanup: DELETE /api/model-endpoints/{id}.
endpoints.bad_input: Omit base_url entirely → 422 (required Form field). base_url present but empty → 400 "Base URL is required". require_models=true against a dead URL → 400 "No models found for that provider/key".
endpoints.notes: FORM body, not JSON. Side effects: strips /models|/chat/completions|/v1/messages suffixes, resolves hostname via Tailscale helper, probes network (1-3s) unless skip_probe=true, and if settings.json has no default_endpoint_id it SETS default_endpoint_id/default_model globally. shared=false stamps owner=caller. Invalidates model caches.

endpoints.purpose: Fast parallel reachability check of LOCAL (private/loopback/Tailscale-CGNAT) endpoints only; 8s result cache
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session; optionally a ModelEndpoint with a private base_url (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1). GET /api/model-endpoints/probe-local. Expect 200 with a dict keyed by endpoint id: {"<ep_id>": {"alive": true, "latency_ms": 42, "status_code": 200, "error": null}}. With no local endpoints, expect 200 {}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session: 403 {"detail": "Admin only"}.
endpoints.notes: Cloud endpoints are skipped (assumed up). 2.5s probe per endpoint via /models (Ollama /api/tags fallback). Result cached 8s in-process.

endpoints.purpose: Dry-run probe of a base_url + api_key without creating a row
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/model-endpoints/test form data: base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 (api_key optional). Expect 200 {"base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1", "online": bool, "status": "online"|"empty"|"offline", "ping_error": <str|null>, "models": [...], "count": <int>}. A dead URL still returns 200 with status "offline".
endpoints.bad_input: Empty base_url → 400 "Base URL is required"; missing field → 422.
endpoints.notes: No DB writes. Network probe 2-3s timeout. Pointing it at Odysseus itself returns a helpful ping_error about using the Ollama URL.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one model endpoint and scrub all settings/chat-sessions referencing it
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + a throwaway endpoint created via POST /api/model-endpoints (skip_probe=true). DELETE /api/model-endpoints/<ep_id>. Expect 200 {"deleted": true, "cleared_settings": [], "cleared_sessions": 0, "cleared_loaded_sessions": 0} (lists/counts non-zero if the endpoint was referenced). Verify GET /api/model-endpoints no longer contains the id.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown ep_id → 404 "Endpoint not found".
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD, but with cascading side effects: clears settings.json fields (default/utility/research/task model + TTS) that point at it and blanks endpoint_url/model/headers on any DB + in-memory chat sessions using that base URL. Invalidates caches. Use a dedicated fixture endpoint, not a shared one.

endpoints.purpose: Toggle is_enabled (no body) or field-update name/model_type/is_enabled/supports_tools (JSON body)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + endpoint id. (a) PATCH /api/model-endpoints/<ep_id> with no body → 200 {"id":...,"is_enabled": <flipped bool>, "supports_tools":..., "name":..., "model_type":...}. (b) PATCH with JSON {"name": "renamed", "is_enabled": true, "supports_tools": true} → 200 reflecting the new values.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown ep_id → 404 "Endpoint not found".
endpoints.notes: Malformed/empty JSON body silently degrades to the legacy toggle behavior. Invalidates model cache. PATCH absent from CORS allow_methods (browser cross-origin only issue).

endpoints.purpose: List human-readable settings labels (Default Model, Utility Model, Deep Research, Background Tasks, Text to Speech) that reference this endpoint
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. GET /api/model-endpoints/<ep_id>/dependents (works even for nonexistent ids — it only inspects settings.json). Expect 200 {"dependents": []} normally, or e.g. {"dependents": ["Default Model"]} when settings.default_endpoint_id == ep_id.
endpoints.notes: Read-only on settings.json; no 404 for unknown ids.

endpoints.purpose: List all discovered models for one endpoint with per-model hidden/visible state (live probe, cached fallback)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + endpoint id (ideally with cached_models populated). GET /api/model-endpoints/<ep_id>/models. Expect 200 array: [{"id": "llama3.2:1b", "display": "llama3.2:1b", "is_hidden": false}, ...]. Offline endpoint with cached models still returns the cached list; offline with no cache returns [].
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown ep_id → 404 "Endpoint not found".
endpoints.notes: Attempts a 3s live network probe first and updates cached_models on success (DB write); falls back to cached list.

endpoints.purpose: Bulk-set the hidden models list for an endpoint
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + endpoint id. PATCH /api/model-endpoints/<ep_id>/models with JSON {"hidden": ["some-model-id"]}. Expect 200 {"id": "<ep_id>", "hidden_count": 1}. Send {"hidden": []} to unhide all (hidden_count 0). Verify via GET .../models that is_hidden flipped.
endpoints.bad_input: {"hidden": "not-a-list"} → 400 "hidden must be a list of model IDs"; unknown ep_id → 404.
endpoints.notes: DB write + model-cache invalidation. PATCH is missing from CORS allow_methods in app.py — curl/same-origin fine, cross-origin browser preflight would fail.

endpoints.purpose: List available chat models grouped by configured ModelEndpoint, owner-scoped per user, cached 30s
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: at least one enabled ModelEndpoint row (create via POST /api/model-endpoints as admin, e.g. local Ollama). Request: GET /api/models?refresh=true with a logged-in session cookie. Expect 200 with {"hosts": [], "items": [{"host":"custom","port":0,"url":"http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions","models":[...],"models_display":[...],"models_extra":[...],"endpoint_id":"<8-char id>","endpoint_name":...,"category":"local"|"api","model_type":"llm"}]}. Offline endpoints appear with "offline": true and empty models.
endpoints.bad_input: Anonymous request (no cookie) in a configured deployment: 401 {"error": "Not authenticated"} from middleware (handler also raises 401 if auth_manager.is_configured).
endpoints.notes: Per-(owner,is_admin) 30s cache; ?refresh=true bypasses. Cache miss kicks off a daemon background thread that re-probes ALL enabled endpoints over the network (2s timeout each, parallel, backs off endpoints failing 3+ times in 5 min). Admins see all endpoints; users see own + null-owner shared.

endpoints.purpose: Probe every enabled endpoint's model-list URL sequentially and report online/offline + latency + model_count
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: admin session + >=1 enabled ModelEndpoint. GET /api/ping. Expect 200 {"endpoints": [{"id":...,"name":...,"base_url":...,"provider":"openai"|"ollama"|"anthropic"|...,"category":"local"|"api","latency_ms":<int|null>,"status":"online"|"offline","model_count":<int>}]}. Unreachable endpoints get status "offline" with an "error" string.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-admin session: 403 Admin only.
endpoints.notes: Sequential httpx GETs with 5s timeout each — with many dead endpoints this approaches the global 45s REQUEST_HARD_TIMEOUT (this path is NOT timeout-exempt). Anthropic endpoints get a bare connectivity GET and hardcoded model count.

endpoints.purpose: Get all of the calling user's preferences (JSON-file-backed key/value store)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/prefs with a logged-in session. Expect 200 with a dict of prefs (possibly {} for a fresh user). After PUT /api/prefs/theme {"value":"dark"}, expect {"theme": "dark", ...}.
endpoints.notes: Backed by data/user_prefs.json; per-user under "_users" when auth enabled, flat legacy format otherwise. Route path is the bare prefix (declared as @router.get("")).

endpoints.purpose: Get one preference value for the calling user
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/prefs/theme with a logged-in session. Expect 200 {"key": "theme", "value": "dark"} after setting it, or {"key": "theme", "value": null} when unset (still 200, never 404).
endpoints.notes: Missing keys return value null, not an error.

endpoints.purpose: Set one preference value for the calling user
endpoints.test_plan: PUT /api/prefs/theme with JSON {"value": "dark"} and a logged-in session. Expect 200 {"key": "theme", "value": "dark"}. Round-trip with GET /api/prefs/theme. Value can be any JSON type (string/number/object/list).
endpoints.bad_input: Non-object body (e.g. "dark" or [1,2]) → 422 (handler requires body: dict). Body {} sets the pref to null (200).
endpoints.notes: Persists to data/user_prefs.json. No key whitelist — arbitrary keys accepted. default_endpoint_id / default_model prefs here feed GET /api/default-chat for non-admin users.

endpoints.purpose: Return all presets known to the preset manager
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/presets with a logged-in session. Expect 200 with the preset_manager.presets dict (includes the built-in/custom preset definitions; exact keys depend on presets file). Just assert 200 + JSON object.
endpoints.notes: Read-only, no handler auth beyond middleware.

endpoints.purpose: Update the single 'custom' character preset (name, temperature, max_tokens, system_prompt, inject prefix/suffix, enabled)
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/presets/custom with JSON {"name": "Pirate", "enabled": true, "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 512, "system_prompt": "You are a pirate.", "inject_prefix": "", "inject_suffix": ""} (all fields have defaults; {} is also valid). Expect 200 {"success": true, "message": "Custom preset updated"}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"temperature": 3.0} → 422 (le=2.0); max_tokens > 8192 → 422; name > 50 chars → 422.
endpoints.notes: Admin enforced via Depends(require_admin). Persists via preset_manager; a manager save failure returns 200 {"success": false}, exceptions → 500.

endpoints.purpose: Get saved group-chat presets
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/presets/groups with a logged-in session. Expect 200 {"groups": [...]} (empty list on fresh install; round-trips whatever POST /api/presets/groups saved).
endpoints.notes: Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: Replace the saved group-chat presets list
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/presets/groups with JSON {"groups": [{"name": "Trio", "members": ["a", "b"]}]}. Expect 200 {"ok": true}. Verify GET /api/presets/groups returns the same groups. Restore with {"groups": []}.
endpoints.bad_input: Non-JSON body → 400/422 from request.json() parse failure; {} is accepted (saves empty list — data.get("groups", [])).
endpoints.notes: No schema validation on group entries — whatever list is sent gets persisted verbatim. Replaces (not merges) existing groups; snapshot/restore in tests.

endpoints.purpose: List user-saved character templates
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/presets/templates with a logged-in session. Expect 200 JSON array (possibly []). After POST a template, expect it to appear with its generated id.
endpoints.notes: Read endpoint has no admin gate; writes do.

endpoints.purpose: Create or update (when id supplied) a user character template
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/presets/templates with JSON {"id": "", "name": "Test Bot", "system_prompt": "You are helpful.", "temperature": 1.0, "max_tokens": 0}. Expect 200 {"success": true, "template": {"id": "user-<8 hex>", "name": "Test Bot", ...}}. Save the returned id for the DELETE test.
endpoints.bad_input: {"name": ""} → 422 (min_length=1); temperature outside 0-2 or max_tokens outside 0-65536 → 422.
endpoints.notes: id "" auto-generates "user-{hex8}"; passing an existing id updates that template.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one user character template
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: create a template via POST /api/presets/templates and capture template.id. DELETE /api/presets/templates/user-<hex8> as admin. Expect 200 {"success": true}. Verify it's gone from GET /api/presets/templates.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown template_id → 200 {"success": false, "message": "Failed to delete template"} (no 404).
endpoints.notes: Ordinary delete-one CRUD; failure signaled in body, not status code.

endpoints.purpose: Return provider list from the model_discovery service, cached 30s globally
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/providers with any logged-in session. Expect 200 with the model_discovery.get_providers() payload (provider/host list). Pass ?refresh=true to bypass the 30s shared cache. Verify second call within 30s returns identical body (cached).
endpoints.notes: No handler-level auth (middleware-only). Underlying discover can port-scan a configured LLM host and take seconds on cache miss; cache is global (not per-user).

endpoints.purpose: List all agent tool tags with enabled/disabled status from settings
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/tools with any logged-in session. Expect 200 {"tools": [{"id": "<tool-tag>", "enabled": true}, ...]} sorted by tag; tags listed in settings.disabled_tools come back enabled:false.
endpoints.notes: No handler-level auth (middleware-only). Reads src.agent_tools.TOOL_TAGS + settings.json.

endpoints.purpose: Set the global disabled-tools list
endpoints.test_plan: Admin session. POST /api/tools with JSON {"disabled": ["web_search"]} → 200 {"ok": true, "disabled": ["web_search"]}. Verify GET /api/tools now shows web_search enabled:false. Restore with {"disabled": []}.
endpoints.bad_input: {"disabled": "web_search"} (string not list) → 422 pydantic validation error.
endpoints.notes: Writes settings.json globally — affects all users' agent runs; restore original value after testing.

endpoints.purpose: List the current user's in-flight (status=running) deep-research tasks held in process memory
endpoints.test_plan: Login (session cookie), then GET /api/research/active. Expect 200 {"active": []} on a fresh instance; after POST /api/research/start, expect one entry with session_id (rp-<12hex>), query, status=running, progress{}, started_at.
endpoints.bad_input: No session cookie -> 401 {"error":"Not authenticated"} from middleware (or 401 'Not authenticated' from _require_user).
endpoints.notes: Reads only research_handler._active_tasks (in-memory), filtered by owner. Completed/persisted research does not appear here.

endpoints.purpose: Cancel a running research task
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a running task started via POST /api/research/start by the same user. POST /api/research/cancel/<sid> with empty body -> 200 {"cancelled": true}. Calling again (already cancelled) -> 200 {"cancelled": false}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown session id -> 404 {"detail":"No research found for this session"}.
endpoints.notes: Only cancels in-memory tasks with status=running; with a disk-only (finished) fixture the ownership check passes but cancel_research returns false -> {"cancelled": false}. Sets task status to cancelled.

endpoints.purpose: Return the full persisted JSON of one research (sources, summary, stats) for the Library preview
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned disk JSON. GET /api/research/detail/<sid> -> 200 returning the raw JSON object (query, result, sources, owner, etc.).
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown or other-user sid -> 404 {"detail":"Research not found"} (404 not 403, deliberately).
endpoints.notes: Response includes the owner field and full report text; corrupted JSON -> 500.

endpoints.purpose: List completed research reports for the Library panel (search/sort/limit/archived filters)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/research/library?sort=recent&limit=50&archived=false -> 200 {"research": [...], "total": N}. With the disk fixture present, expect an item with id=<sid>, query, category, source_count, status, duration, rounds, started_at, completed_at, archived:false. Also try ?search=test (substring match on query, case-insensitive) and sort values recent|oldest|most-messages|alpha.
endpoints.bad_input: limit=abc -> 422 (int query param validation).
endpoints.notes: Scans data/deep_research/*.json; rows without owner == current user are hidden (legacy ownerless JSONs never show). archived=true shows ONLY archived items.

endpoints.purpose: Render and serve the visual HTML report for a completed research session
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: data/deep_research/<sid>.json owned by the user with query/result (and optionally sources, stats, category). GET /api/research/report/<sid> -> 200, Content-Type text/html, body is a full HTML report page.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown session id -> 404 {"detail":"Research not found"} (ownership gate) ; existing JSON but report generation failure -> 404 "No visual report available for this session" or 500.
endpoints.notes: Returns HTMLResponse not JSON. Generated fresh each call from the JSON via src/visual_report.generate_visual_report; respects hidden_images list.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch research result + sources + raw findings WITHOUT consuming/clearing it (panel use)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned disk JSON with result set. POST /api/research/result-peek/<sid> (empty body) -> 200 {"result":"# Report","sources":[],"raw_findings":[],"category":""}. Safe to call repeatedly — preferred over /result for testing.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown sid -> 404 "No research found for this session"; owned-but-resultless -> 404 "No research result available".
endpoints.notes: Reads in-memory first, falls back to disk JSON. No side effects.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch the finished research result + sources + raw findings, then CLEAR the in-memory result (consume semantics)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: completed research owned by the user (disk JSON as in /status test, with "result" set and no "consumed" flag). POST /api/research/result/<sid> (empty body) -> 200 {"result":"# Report","sources":[],"raw_findings":[]}.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown/foreign session id -> 404 {"detail":"No research result available"}.
endpoints.notes: DESTRUCTIVE-ish consume: calls research_handler.clear_result(sid) after reading — repeat calls may 404 once the result is marked consumed. Use /result-peek for non-consuming reads in test loops.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new chat session pre-seeded with the research report as a system message for follow-up questions
endpoints.test_plan: Prereqs: owned (or any readable) research JSON with a result, AND at least one enabled model endpoint (else 400). POST /api/research/spinoff/<sid> (empty body) -> 200 {"session_id": "<uuid4>", "name": "Follow-up: <query, truncated to 60 chars>", "source_count": N}. Verify the new session exists via the sessions API and contains one system message.
endpoints.bad_input: Sid with no persisted result -> 404 "No research result available for this session"; no endpoints configured -> 400 "No endpoint configured — add one in Settings first".
endpoints.notes: Side effects: creates a persistent chat session owned by the caller, saves sessions, fires session_created event. NOTE: this handler does NOT call _assert_owns_research — it only requires login, so any user with a known sid can spin off another user's report (potential cross-tenant read; worth flagging in audit). Endpoint inheritance: source chat session -> chat -> research -> utility -> first enabled endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Get status/progress of a research task (in-memory first, falls back to persisted JSON for completed runs)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: a file data/deep_research/<sid>.json containing {"owner":"<login-user>","query":"test q","status":"done","started_at":1718000000,"result":"# Report","sources":[]} (or a live task started via /api/research/start). GET /api/research/status/<sid> -> 200 {"status":"done","progress":{},"query":"test q","started_at":...} (running tasks also include avg_duration when history exists).
endpoints.bad_input: GET /api/research/status/nonexistent-id -> 404 {"detail":"No research found for this session"}.
endpoints.notes: Ownership gate _owns_in_memory checks in-memory owner, else the on-disk JSON's owner field; legacy JSONs without owner are invisible (404). Disk JSONs with "consumed":true return 404.

endpoints.purpose: Delete one research result JSON from disk (ordinary delete-one CRUD)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned disk JSON (use a throwaway copy). DELETE /api/research/<sid> -> 200 {"deleted": true}. Repeat -> 200 {"deleted": false} (file gone, no error).
endpoints.bad_input: Sid owned by another user or unreadable JSON -> 404 {"detail":"Research not found"}.
endpoints.notes: Nonexistent file is NOT a 404 — returns {"deleted": false}. Run after all other tests against that fixture.

endpoints.purpose: Soft-archive or restore a research report (sets archived flag in its JSON)
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned disk JSON. POST /api/research/<sid>/archive?archived=true (empty body) -> 200 {"ok":true,"id":"<sid>","archived":true}. Restore with ?archived=false. Verify via /api/research/library?archived=true.
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown sid -> 404 {"detail":"Research not found"}; archived=notabool -> 422.
endpoints.notes: archived is a QUERY param defaulting to true, not a body field. Rewrites the JSON file.

endpoints.purpose: Persist an image URL into the research JSON's hidden_images list so /report skips it
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned research JSON on disk. POST /api/research/<sid>/hide-image with JSON {"url": "https://example.com/img.png"} -> 200 {"ok": true}. Verify the JSON file now contains hidden_images:["https://example.com/img.png"].
endpoints.bad_input: Missing "url" field in body -> 422 pydantic validation error; unknown sid -> 404 "Research not found".
endpoints.notes: Mutates data/deep_research/<sid>.json on disk. Idempotent for the same URL.

endpoints.purpose: Clear the hidden_images list for a research session
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: owned research JSON (ideally with hidden_images set via hide-image). POST /api/research/<sid>/unhide-images, empty body -> 200 {"ok": true}; JSON file's hidden_images becomes [].
endpoints.bad_input: Unknown session id -> 404 {"detail":"Research not found"}.
endpoints.notes: Disk mutation only; safe to call repeatedly.

endpoints.purpose: Standalone web search via the configured provider chain; returns a context string plus source list (used by Compare mode)
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/search with JSON {"query": "latest python release"} (also accepts form data or ?query=; 'q' and 'freshness'/'time_filter' aliases work) -> 200 {"context": "<text>", "sources": [{...}]}. If no provider is reachable, still 200 but {"context":"","sources":[],"error":"<msg>"} — assert on absence of the error key for the happy path.
endpoints.bad_input: Empty/missing query -> 200 {"context":"","sources":[],"error":"query is required"} (never 4xx).
endpoints.notes: Needs a working search provider: default searxng requires a configured instance URL (admin setting search_url or SEARXNG env); duckduckgo needs no key; brave/google_pse/tavily/serper need API keys (settings or BRAVE/GOOGLE_API_KEY/TAVILY_API_KEY/SERPER_API_KEY env). All failures are wrapped into a 200 envelope with 'error'. Subject to the global 45s request timeout. _request_values deliberately accepts JSON, form, and query params.

endpoints.purpose: Return current search configuration (active provider, has_api_key, result_count, search_url for searxng)
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/search/config with session cookie -> 200 JSON like {"primary_provider":"searxng","active_provider":"searxng","has_api_key":false,"result_count":<int>,"search_url":"<instance or ''>"} (search_url only when provider is searxng).
endpoints.bad_input: No session cookie -> 401 from auth middleware.
endpoints.notes: No per-route auth check — relies entirely on the global AuthMiddleware. Read-only.

endpoints.purpose: List selectable search providers with availability based on configured keys/instance URL
endpoints.test_plan: GET /api/search/providers -> 200 JSON array (top-level list, not object) of {"id","label","available"} for searxng, brave, duckduckgo, google_pse, tavily, serper ('disabled' is excluded). duckduckgo should always have available:true; key-requiring providers show false until keys are set.
endpoints.notes: Read-only; availability computed from admin settings/env, no network calls.

endpoints.purpose: Search using one explicit provider (compare-search mode), returning raw result list with timing
endpoints.test_plan: POST /api/search/query with JSON {"query": "fastapi tutorial", "provider": "duckduckgo", "count": 5} (form/query-param input also accepted; 'limit' aliases count, capped at 20, default 10) -> 200 {"results": [{title,url,...}], "provider": "duckduckgo", "time": <float secs>}. Provider failure -> 200 with results:[] and error string.
endpoints.bad_input: {"query":"x","provider":"bing"} -> 200 {"results":[],"provider":"bing","error":"Unknown provider"}; missing query -> 200 {"results":[],"provider":"...","error":"query is required"}. Non-numeric count silently falls back to 10.
endpoints.notes: Calls _call_provider directly (no fallback chain, no cache). Provider 'searxng' needs the instance URL; keyed providers need their API keys; duckduckgo is the credential-free happy path. Always 200, never raises.

endpoints.purpose: Keyword-frequency topic analysis across the user's non-archived sessions (Technology, Science, Work, ...).
endpoints.test_plan: Fixture: own session whose messages contain topic keywords (e.g. 'python code'). curl -b cookies.txt http://HOST/api/conversations/topics. Expect 200 with topic frequency data (topics list with counts and per-topic match excerpts referencing session_id/session_name/role).
endpoints.bad_input: Internal analyzer failure -> 500 'Topic analysis failed: ...'.
endpoints.notes: Pure keyword matching in src/topic_analyzer.py — NO LLM call, no token spend. Strict owner filtering; iterates in-memory sessions only.

endpoints.purpose: history_routes version: rich history (filters hidden messages, DB fallback, returns model/endpoint_url/name/crew_member_id) — SHADOWED and unreachable.
endpoints.test_plan: Cannot be exercised over HTTP as mounted: session_routes registers the identical path first (app.py line 500 vs 528), so all requests to GET /api/history/<sid> hit the session_routes handler and return {"history": [...]} only. To test this handler's logic (hidden-message filtering, DB fallback) it must be invoked directly in unit tests or the duplicate must be removed.
endpoints.bad_input: n/a (unreachable).
